title.zh: 卷三百三十八 列傳第九十七 蘇軾子:過
title.en: Volume 338 Biographies 97: Su Shi and son: Guo
title.raw: 卷三百三十八 列傳第九十七 蘇軾子:過 Volume 338 Biographies 97: Su Shi and son: Guo

sentences.zh: 蘇軾，字子瞻，眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Su Shi, styled Zizhan, was a native of Meishan in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi, whose style name was Zizhan, came from Meishan in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 生十年，父洵遊學四方，母程氏親授以書，聞古今成敗，輒能語其要。

translations.literal: By the age of ten, his father Xun was traveling to study in all directions, and his mother, Lady Cheng, personally taught him books; when she spoke of successes and failures in past and present, he could always state their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: When he was ten, his father Su Xun was away studying throughout the realm, while his mother Lady Cheng taught him herself; whenever she discussed the rise and fall of men and states in history, he could summarize the main points.

sentences.zh: 程氏讀東漢《范滂傳》，慨然太息，軾請曰：「軾若爲滂，母許之否乎？」

translations.literal: Lady Cheng was reading the Eastern Han biography of Fan Pang and sighed deeply with emotion; Shi asked, "If I were to be like Pang, would you permit it, Mother?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cheng was reading the Eastern Han account of Fan Pang and sighed with deep feeling. Shi asked her, "Mother, if I were to be like Fan Pang, would you allow it?"

sentences.zh: 程氏曰：「汝能爲滂，吾顧不能爲滂母邪？」

translations.literal: Lady Cheng said, "If you can be like Pang, could I not be like Pang's mother?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cheng replied, "If you can be like Fan Pang, why should I not be like Fan Pang's mother?"

sentences.zh: 比冠，博通經史，屬文日數千言，好賈誼、陸贄書。

translations.literal: By the time he reached manhood, he was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories, composed essays of several thousand words a day, and loved the writings of Jia Yi and Lu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he came of age, he had mastered the classics and histories, wrote several thousand words of prose a day, and favored the works of Jia Yi and Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 旣而讀《莊子》，歎曰：「吾昔有見，口未能言，今見是書，得吾心矣。」

translations.literal: Later, when he read the Zhuangzi, he sighed and said, "I had insights before but could not put them into words; now, seeing this book, I have found what is in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Later, reading the Zhuangzi, he exclaimed, "I had seen these truths before but could not express them; now this book has found the words for what I felt."

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，試禮部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, he took the Ministry of Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1057 he sat for the metropolitan examination at the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 方時文磔裂詭異之弊勝，主司歐陽脩思有以救之，得軾《刑賞忠厚論》，驚喜，欲擢冠多士，猶疑其客曾鞏所爲，但置第二；

translations.literal: At that time the fault of fractured, bizarre examination prose prevailed; the chief examiner Ouyang Xiu wished to remedy it. He received Shi's "On Punishments and Rewards with Generous Sincerity," was delighted and astonished, and wished to place him first among all candidates, but still suspected it was the work of his protégé Zeng Gong, and so ranked him only second.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary examination essays were dominated by fractured, eccentric prose, and chief examiner Ouyang Xiu sought a remedy. When he read Shi's "On Punishments and Rewards with Generous Sincerity," he was thrilled and meant to rank him first among all candidates, yet still suspected the essay might be the work of his protégé Zeng Gong, so he placed Shi second.

sentences.zh: 復以《春秋》對義居第一，殿試中乙科。

translations.literal: He again ranked first in the Spring and Autumn exegesis examination and passed the palace examination in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: He again placed first in the Spring and Autumn exegesis test and received the second rank in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 後以書見脩，脩語梅聖俞曰：「吾當避此人出一頭地。」

translations.literal: Later he presented a letter to Xiu; Xiu said to Mei Shengyu, "I ought to yield and let this man stand out a head above others."
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent a letter to Ouyang Xiu, who told Mei Shengyu, "I ought to step aside and let this man rise a head above the rest."

sentences.zh: 聞者始譁不厭，久乃信服。

translations.literal: Those who heard this at first clamored in displeasure, but in time they came to believe and accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard this remark at first protested loudly, but in time they came to accept it.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 五年，調福昌主簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was assigned as registrar of Fuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he was appointed registrar of Fuchang.

sentences.zh: 歐陽脩以才識兼茂，薦之秘閣。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu recommended him to the Secretariat Pavilion on the grounds that his talent and learning were both outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu recommended him for the Secretariat Pavilion, citing his exceptional talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 試六論，舊不起草，以故文多不工。

translations.literal: In the trial of six discursive essays, candidates had formerly not prepared drafts, and for this reason most compositions were poorly wrought.
translations.idiomatic: In the six-essay examination, candidates had traditionally not drafted their work beforehand, so most essays were poorly finished.

sentences.zh: 軾始具草，文義粲然。

translations.literal: Shi was the first to prepare a full draft, and his argument and language were brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was the first to submit a full draft, and his argument shone with clarity.

sentences.zh: 復對制策，入三等。

translations.literal: He again answered the policy questions and entered the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: He again sat for the policy examination and was placed in the third grade.

sentences.zh: 自宋初以來，制策入三等，惟吳育與軾而已。

translations.literal: Since the beginning of the Song, only Wu Yu and Shi had entered the third grade in the policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the Song, only Wu Yu and Shi had achieved the third grade in the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 除大理評事、簽書鳳翔府判官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and signing secretary to the administrative assistant of Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and signing secretary to the Fengxiang prefectural judge.

sentences.zh: 關中自元昊叛，民貧役重，岐下歲輸南山木筏，自渭入河，經砥柱之險，衙吏踵破家。

translations.literal: Since Yuanhao's rebellion in Guanzhong, the people had been poor and corvée burdens heavy; below Qi, timber rafts from the southern mountains were delivered yearly, entering the river from the Wei and passing the peril of Jizhi, and yamen clerks in succession ruined their families.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanhao's rebellion, Guanzhong was impoverished and corvée burdens were crushing. Each year timber rafts from the southern mountains were sent downstream from Qi, entering the Wei and then the Yellow River and passing the treacherous Jizhi rapids, and yamen clerks were ruined one after another.

sentences.zh: 軾訪其利害，爲脩衙規，使自擇水工以時進止，自是害減半。

translations.literal: Shi investigated the advantages and harms, drew up regulations for the yamen transport service, and had them choose water workers themselves to advance or halt according to season; from this the harm was reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Shi investigated the costs and benefits, drafted regulations for the transport office, and allowed clerks to choose their own river hands and time their departures accordingly; from then on the losses were cut in half.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，入判登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping he entered service as judge of the Petition Drum Court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1065 he was appointed judge of the Petition Drum Court.

sentences.zh: 英宗自藩邸聞其名，欲以唐故事召入翰林，知制誥。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong had heard his name while still in the princely residence and wished, following Tang precedent, to summon him into the Hanlin Academy as drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Emperor Yingzong had heard of him and wished, following Tang precedent, to summon him to the Hanlin Academy as drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 宰相韓琦曰：「軾之才，遠大器也，他日自當爲天下用。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Han Qi said, "Shi's talent is that of a vessel for great distant use; in time he will naturally serve the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Han Qi said, "Shi is a man of great capacity meant for the long term; in time he will naturally serve the empire.

sentences.zh: 要在朝廷培養之，使天下之士莫不畏慕降伏，皆欲朝廷進用，然後取而用之，則人人無復異辭矣。

translations.literal: The essential thing is to cultivate him at court so that scholars throughout the realm all fear, admire, and submit to him and all wish the court to advance him; only then take and employ him, and then no one will have further dissenting words.
translations.idiomatic: The court should cultivate him so that scholars everywhere admire him and long for his advancement; only then should he be appointed, and no one will object.

sentences.zh: 今驟用之，則天下之士未必以爲然，適足以累之也。」

translations.literal: If he is used abruptly now, scholars throughout the realm may not necessarily approve, and this would only be enough to burden him.
translations.idiomatic: If he is promoted too suddenly, the scholarly world may not accept it, and that would only harm him.

sentences.zh: 英宗曰：「且與脩注如何？」

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong said, "How about giving him a post as chronicler alongside Xiu for now?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong asked, "What if we assign him to work on the veritable records with Ouyang Xiu for now?"

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「記注與制誥爲鄰，未可遽授。

translations.literal: Qi said, "Chronicling and drafting edicts are neighboring offices; it cannot be granted hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi replied, "The chronicle office borders on edict drafting; we cannot grant that post too quickly.

sentences.zh: 不若於館閣中近上貼職與之，且請召試。」

translations.literal: It would be better to give him an attached post in the academies close to the throne, and also request a summoned examination.
translations.idiomatic: Better to give him an attached post in the palace academies close to the throne, and call for an examination.

sentences.zh: 英宗曰：「試之未知其能否，如軾有不能邪？」

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong said, "Testing would not yet reveal whether he can do it; could Shi possibly be unable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "An examination might not show his ability—but could Shi possibly fail?"

sentences.zh: 琦猶不可，及試二論，復入三等，得直史館。

translations.literal: Qi still would not agree; when he was examined on two essays he again entered the third grade and received appointment as compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi still objected, but when Shi was examined on two essays he again achieved the third grade and was appointed compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 軾聞琦語，曰：「公可謂愛人以德矣。」

translations.literal: When Shi heard Qi's words, he said, "Your Grace may truly be said to love a man by honoring virtue."
translations.idiomatic: When Shi heard Han Qi's reasoning, he remarked, "Your Grace truly loves a man by honoring his virtue."

sentences.zh: 會洵卒，賻以金帛，辭之，求贈一官，於是贈光祿丞。

translations.literal: At this time Xun died; condolence gifts of gold and silk were sent, which he declined, requesting instead the grant of an office, and so Xun was posthumously given the rank of Vice Director of the Imperial Livery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Su Xun died. The court offered gold and silk as condolence gifts, but Shi declined them and asked that an office be granted to his father instead; Xun was then posthumously given the rank of Vice Director of the Imperial Livery.

sentences.zh: 洵將終，以兄太白早亡，子孫未立，妹嫁杜氏，卒未葬，屬軾。

translations.literal: As Xun was about to die, he noted that his elder brother Taibai had died early, his descendants were not established, and his sister, married to the Du clan, had died and was still unburied; he entrusted these matters to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Xun told Shi that his elder brother Taibai had died young without heirs, and that his sister, married into the Du family, had died and remained unburied; he charged Shi with these duties.

sentences.zh: 軾旣除喪，卽葬姑。

translations.literal: After Shi had completed mourning, he at once buried his aunt.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as his mourning period ended, Shi buried his aunt.

sentences.zh: 後官可蔭，推與太白曾孫彭。

translations.literal: Later, when an office could be obtained by hereditary privilege, he yielded it to Taibai's great-grandson Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he became eligible for a privilege appointment, he gave it to Taibai's great-grandson Peng.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，還朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1069 he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 王安石執政，素惡其議論異己，以判官告院。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi held power and had long disliked his opinions as differing from his own; he was made judge of the Office for Reporting Matters.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Anshi in power, who had long resented Shi's dissenting views, Shi was assigned as judge of the Office for Reporting Matters.

sentences.zh: 四年，安石欲變科舉、興學校，詔兩制、三館議。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Anshi wished to change the civil service examinations and establish schools; an edict ordered the two drafting corps and the three institutes to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1071 Wang Anshi proposed reforming the examinations and expanding the schools, and the emperor ordered the drafting corps and palace institutes to submit opinions.

sentences.zh: 軾上議曰：

translations.literal: Shi submitted a memorial of deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shi submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 「得人之道，在於知人；

translations.literal: "The way to obtain men lies in knowing men;
translations.idiomatic: "The way to find good men lies in knowing men;

sentences.zh: 知人之法，在於責實。

translations.literal: the method of knowing men lies in holding them to real achievement.
translations.idiomatic: and the method of knowing men lies in holding them accountable for real results.

sentences.zh: 使君相有知人之明，朝廷有責實之政，則胥吏皂隸未嘗無人，而況于學校貢舉乎？

translations.literal: If ruler and minister have the discernment to know men and the court has a policy of holding to real achievement, then even clerks and runners have never lacked capable men—how much more so for schools and the examination system?
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler and his ministers know how to judge talent and the court demands real achievement, even petty clerks yield capable men—how much more will schools and examinations?

sentences.zh: 雖因今之法，臣以爲有餘。

translations.literal: Even following the present laws, your subject believes there is more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: Even under the present system, I believe that would be more than enough.

sentences.zh: 使君相不知人，朝廷不責實，則公卿侍從常患無人，而況學校貢舉乎？

translations.literal: If ruler and minister do not know men and the court does not hold to real achievement, then high ministers and attendants constantly worry that there are no men—how much more so for schools and the examination system?
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler and his ministers cannot judge talent and the court does not demand real results, even the highest offices lack good men—how much less will schools and examinations supply them?

sentences.zh: 雖復古之制，臣以爲不足。

translations.literal: Even if ancient institutions were restored, your subject believes it would not be enough.
translations.idiomatic: Even restoring ancient institutions would not suffice.

sentences.zh: 夫時有可否，物有廢興，方其所安，雖暴君不能廢，及其旣厭，雖聖人不能復。

translations.literal: Times have what may or may not be done; things have what is abandoned or revived. While people are at ease with them, even a tyrant cannot abolish them; once they have grown weary of them, even a sage cannot restore them.
translations.idiomatic: What works in one age fails in another; customs rise and fall. While people are content with a practice, even a tyrant cannot abolish it; once they tire of it, even a sage cannot bring it back.

sentences.zh: 故風俗之變，法制隨之，譬如江河之徙移，強而復之，則難爲力。

translations.literal: Therefore as customs change, laws and institutions follow them, like the shifting of rivers—if one forcibly restores the old course, it is hard to apply strength.
translations.idiomatic: Customs change and institutions must follow, like a river changing its course—forcing it back is nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 慶曆固嘗立學矣，至于今日，惟有空名僅存。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era schools were indeed established, but down to today only empty names barely remain.
translations.idiomatic: Schools were established in the Qingli reforms, yet today only empty titles remain.

sentences.zh: 今將變今之禮，易今之俗，又當發民力以治宮室，斂民財以食遊士。

translations.literal: Now you will change present rites and alter present customs, and moreover must mobilize the people's labor to build palaces and halls and gather the people's wealth to feed roaming scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Now you propose to change present rites and alter present customs, mobilize the people's labor to build schools, and tax their wealth to support idle scholars.

sentences.zh: 百里之內，置官立師，獄訟聽於是，軍旅謀於是，又簡不率教者屏之遠方，則無乃徒爲紛亂，以患苦天下邪？

translations.literal: Within a hundred li you will set up officials and appoint teachers, hear lawsuits there and plan military affairs there, and moreover select those who do not follow instruction and banish them to distant regions—will this not merely create confusion and afflict the realm with hardship?
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred li you will place officials and teachers, hold lawsuits and plan campaigns in the schools, and exile students who fail to obey—will this not only spread disorder and bring hardship on the realm?

sentences.zh: 若乃無大更革，而望有益於時，則與慶曆之際何異？

translations.literal: If there is no great reform and yet you hope for benefit to the age, how is this different from the Qingli period?
translations.idiomatic: If there is no real reform yet you expect benefit to the age, how will this differ from the Qingli experiment?

sentences.zh: 故臣謂今之學校，特可因仍舊制，使先王之舊物，不廢於吾世足矣。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject says that for present schools it is enough merely to follow the old system and keep the former kings' institutions from being abandoned in our age.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore hold that the schools need only follow the old system so that the institutions of the former kings are not lost in our age.

sentences.zh: 至於貢舉之法，行之百年，治亂盛衰，初不由此。

translations.literal: As for the examination system, it has been practiced for a century; order and disorder, rise and decline, have never in the first place depended on this.
translations.idiomatic: As for the examination system, practiced for a century, the rise and fall of dynasties has never depended on it.

sentences.zh: 陛下視祖宗之世，貢舉之法，與今爲孰精？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, consider the age of the ancestral emperors: was the examination system then or now the more refined?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, compare the examination system of the ancestral emperors' age with today's—which was finer?

sentences.zh: 言語文章，與今爲孰優？

translations.literal: Were speech and literary composition then or now the superior?
translations.idiomatic: Were literary composition and eloquence then or now superior?

sentences.zh: 所得人才，與今爲孰多？

translations.literal: Were the talented men obtained then or now the more numerous?
translations.idiomatic: Were the talented men produced then or now more numerous?

sentences.zh: 天下之事，與今爲孰辦？

translations.literal: Were affairs under Heaven then or now the better managed?
translations.idiomatic: Were affairs of state then or now the better managed?

sentences.zh: 較此四者之長短，其議決矣。

translations.literal: Compare the strengths and weaknesses of these four matters, and the deliberation is decided.
translations.idiomatic: Compare these four points, and the debate is settled.

sentences.zh: 今所欲變改不過數端：或曰鄉舉德行而略文詞，或曰專取策論而罷詩賦，或欲兼采譽望而罷封彌，或欲經生不帖墨而考大義，此皆知其一，不知其二者也。

translations.literal: The changes now proposed are only a few items: some say recommend virtue in local selection and slight literary composition; some say take policy essays exclusively and abolish poetry and rhapsody; some wish to combine reputation with abolishing sealed copies; some wish classical scholars not to copy passages but to be examined on great principles—these all know one side and do not know both.
translations.idiomatic: The proposed changes are only a few: recommend virtue in local selection and slight literary skill; take policy essays alone and abolish poetry; combine reputation with open examination; test classical scholars on principles rather than transcription—all know one side and not both.

sentences.zh: 願陛下留意于遠者、大者，區區之法何預焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, I hope you will attend to what is distant and great; what have petty methods to do with this?
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to attend to what is far-reaching and great; petty regulations are beside the point.

sentences.zh: 臣又切有私憂過計者。

translations.literal: Your subject also has a private worry that may be excessive calculation.
translations.idiomatic: I also have a personal concern that may be overwrought.

sentences.zh: 夫性命之說，自子貢不得聞，而今之學者，恥不言性命，讀其文，浩然無當而不可窮；

translations.literal: As for doctrines of nature and fate, even Zigong could not hear them from the Master, yet scholars today are ashamed not to speak of nature and fate; read their writings and they are vast and boundless yet without substance and cannot be exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Even Zigong never heard Confucius discuss nature and fate, yet today's scholars are ashamed not to speak of them; read their writings and they seem vast and inexhaustible yet say nothing solid;

sentences.zh: 觀其貌，超然無著而不可挹，此豈真能然哉！

translations.literal: observe their bearing and they seem transcendent, ungraspable, and impossible to draw up—can they truly be so!
translations.idiomatic: observe their bearing and they seem lofty and untouchable—can they truly be so!

sentences.zh: 蓋中人之性，安於放而樂於誕耳。

translations.literal: This is simply the nature of mediocre men, who are at ease in license and take pleasure in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: This is simply the nature of mediocre men, who are comfortable with license and delight in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦安用之？」

translations.literal: Of what use would Your Majesty make them?"
translations.idiomatic: Of what use would Your Majesty make such men?"

sentences.zh: 議上，神宗悟曰：「吾固疑此，得軾議，意釋然矣。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Shenzong understood and said, "I had indeed doubted this; receiving Shi's deliberation, my mind is now at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, Emperor Shenzong said, "I had already doubted this; reading Shi's argument has set my mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 卽日召見，問：「方今政令得失安在？

translations.literal: That very day he summoned him for an audience and asked, "Where do the gains and losses of present government orders lie?
translations.idiomatic: That same day he summoned Shi and asked, "Where do the strengths and weaknesses of present policy lie?

sentences.zh: 雖朕過失，指陳可也。」

translations.literal: Even my own faults—you may point them out."
translations.idiomatic: Even my own faults—you may point them out."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下生知之性，天縱文武，不患不明，不患不勤，不患不斷，但患求治太急，聽言太廣，進人太銳。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty's nature is one of innate knowledge, heaven-endowed in both civil and military affairs; there is no worry about lack of clarity, no worry about lack of diligence, no worry about lack of decisiveness—only worry about seeking order too urgently, listening to words too broadly, and advancing men too sharply.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty's nature is one of innate wisdom, gifted in both civil and military affairs. You need not fear lack of clarity, diligence, or resolve—only that you seek order too urgently, listen to too many voices, and promote men too sharply.

sentences.zh: 願鎮以安靜，待物之來，然後應之。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will steady yourself with calm and quiet, wait for things to come, and then respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to remain calm and quiet, wait for matters to present themselves, and then respond.

sentences.zh: 神宗悚然曰：「卿三言，朕當熟思之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong started and said, "Your three words—I shall ponder them carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said, "Your three warnings—I shall ponder them carefully.

sentences.zh: 凡在館閣，皆當爲朕深思治亂，無有所隱。」

translations.literal: All who are in the academies should deeply ponder order and disorder for me and conceal nothing."
translations.idiomatic: All who serve in the academies should ponder order and disorder for me and conceal nothing."

sentences.zh: 軾退，言於同列。

translations.literal: Shi withdrew and spoke of this to his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi withdrew, he told his colleagues what had passed.

sentences.zh: 安石不悅，命權開封府推官，將困之以事。

translations.literal: Anshi was displeased and ordered him made acting investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefectural court, intending to wear him down with business.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was displeased and appointed him acting investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefectural court, intending to overwhelm him with work.

sentences.zh: 軾決斷精敏，聲聞益遠。

translations.literal: Shi's judgments were keen and sharp, and his reputation spread ever farther.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's judgments were swift and precise, and his reputation spread ever wider.

sentences.zh: 會上元敕府市浙燈，且令損價。

translations.literal: It happened that for the Lantern Festival an edict ordered the prefecture to purchase Zhejiang lanterns and also commanded reduced prices.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lantern Festival the court ordered the prefecture to purchase lanterns from Zhejiang and to force down their prices.

sentences.zh: 軾疏言：「陛下豈以燈爲悅？

translations.literal: Shi submitted a memorial saying, "Does Your Majesty take pleasure in lanterns?
translations.idiomatic: Shi memorialized the throne: "Does Your Majesty take pleasure in lanterns?

sentences.zh: 此不過以奉二宮之歡耳。

translations.literal: This is only to offer joy to the Two Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: This is only to please the empress dowager and the empress.

sentences.zh: 然百姓不可戶曉，皆謂以耳目不急之玩，奪其口體必用之資。

translations.literal: Yet the common people cannot be made to understand household by household; all say that for trifling pleasures not urgent to eye and ear, their resources needed for mouth and body are being seized.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the common people cannot be told household by household; they believe the court is seizing their daily necessities for mere ornaments.

sentences.zh: 此事至小，體則甚大，願追還前命。」

translations.literal: This matter is extremely small, but in principle it is very great; I hope Your Majesty will recall the previous order.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is trifling, but the principle is weighty; I beg Your Majesty to revoke the order.

sentences.zh: 卽詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict at once abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately revoked the order.

sentences.zh: 時安石創行新法，軾上書論其不便，曰：

translations.literal: At this time Anshi was initiating the new laws; Shi submitted a letter discussing their inconveniences, saying:
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Anshi was launching the New Policies, Shi submitted a memorial on their drawbacks, saying:

sentences.zh: 「臣之所欲言者，三言而已。

translations.literal: "What your subject wishes to say is only three words.
translations.idiomatic: "What I wish to say can be summed up in three points.

sentences.zh: 願陛下結人心，厚風俗，存紀綱。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will bind the hearts of the people, enrich customs, and preserve institutions and standards.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to win the people's hearts, strengthen customs, and preserve institutions.

sentences.zh: 人主之所恃者人心而已，如木之有根，燈之有膏，魚之有水，農夫之有田，商賈之有財。

translations.literal: What a ruler relies on is only the hearts of the people, like a tree having roots, a lamp having oil, a fish having water, a farmer having fields, a merchant having wealth.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler relies on nothing but the people's hearts—as a tree needs roots, a lamp needs oil, a fish needs water, a farmer needs fields, a merchant needs capital.

sentences.zh: 失之則亡，此理之必然也。

translations.literal: Lose them and there is ruin—this is the necessary principle.
translations.idiomatic: Lose them and ruin follows—this is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，未有和易同眾而不安，剛果自用而不危者。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present there has never been one who was gentle and easy, in accord with the multitude, yet not secure, or one who was firm and decisive and self-willed yet not in peril.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, no ruler who was gentle and in harmony with the people failed to prosper, and none who was harsh and self-willed escaped danger.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦知人心之不悅矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also knows that hearts are displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already knows that the people are displeased.

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，治財用者不過三司。

translations.literal: Since the ancestral emperors, those who managed finances were none other than the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding emperors, fiscal affairs have been managed by the Three Departments alone.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不以財用付三司，無故又創制置三司條例一司，使六七少年，日夜講求于內，使者四十餘輩，分行營幹於外。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty does not entrust finances to the Three Departments but without cause has again created the Fiscal Planning Commission, setting six or seven youths to pursue schemes day and night within, and more than forty envoys to operate in separate lines outside.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has not entrusted finances to the Three Departments but has created the Fiscal Planning Commission, set six or seven young men to scheme day and night within the palace, and dispatched more than forty agents to operate throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫制置三司條例司，求利之名也；

translations.literal: The Fiscal Planning Commission is a name for seeking profit;
translations.idiomatic: The Fiscal Planning Commission is a name for profit-seeking;

sentences.zh: 六七少年與使者四十餘輩，求利之器也。

translations.literal: the six or seven youths and the more than forty envoys are the instruments of seeking profit.
translations.idiomatic: the six or seven youths and the more than forty agents are its instruments.

sentences.zh: 造端宏大，民實驚疑；

translations.literal: The beginning is vast in scope and the people are truly startled and doubtful;
translations.idiomatic: The enterprise is vast in scope and the people are alarmed and doubtful;

sentences.zh: 創法新奇，吏皆惶惑。

translations.literal: the laws created are novel and strange and officials are all fearful and confused.
translations.idiomatic: the laws are novel and strange, and officials are fearful and confused.

sentences.zh: 以萬乘之主而言利，以天子之宰而治財，論說百端，喧傳萬口，然而莫之顧者，徒曰：『我無其事，何恤於人言。』

translations.literal: For the lord of ten thousand chariots to speak of profit, for the Son of Heaven's minister to manage finances—arguments multiply in a hundred ways and clamor spreads from ten thousand mouths, yet none are heeded; they only say, 'I am not doing this—why worry about people's words?'
translations.idiomatic: For the sovereign of ten thousand chariots to speak of profit and the chief minister to manage finances—arguments multiply and rumor spreads, yet no one heeds the outcry, saying only, 'I am not doing this—why worry what people say?'

sentences.zh: 操網罟而入江湖，語人曰：『我非漁也』，不如捐網罟而人自信。

translations.literal: Take nets and enter rivers and lakes, telling people, 'I am not fishing'—better to cast aside the nets and let people trust of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: It is like taking nets onto the river and saying, 'I am not fishing'—better to cast aside the nets and let people trust you of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 驅鷹犬而赴林藪，語人曰：『我非獵也』，不如放鷹犬而獸自馴。

translations.literal: Drive hawks and hounds into thickets, telling people, 'I am not hunting'—better to release the hawks and hounds and let beasts tame themselves.
translations.idiomatic: It is like driving hawks and hounds into the woods and saying, 'I am not hunting'—better to release them and let the game come of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 故臣以爲欲消讒慝而召和氣，則莫若罷條例司。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject believes that if you wish to dispel slander and malice and summon harmonious qi, there is nothing better than abolishing the Fiscal Planning Commission.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore believe that to dispel slander and restore harmony, nothing is better than abolishing the Fiscal Planning Commission.

sentences.zh: 今君臣宵旰，幾一年矣，而富國之功，茫如捕風，徒聞內帑出數百萬緡，祠部度五千餘人耳。

translations.literal: Now ruler and ministers toil from dusk to dawn, nearly a year has passed, yet the achievement of enriching the state is vague as catching the wind; one only hears that the inner treasury has disbursed several million strings of cash and the Sacrificial Administration has ordained more than five thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly a year ruler and ministers have labored from dawn to dusk, yet the goal of enriching the state remains as elusive as catching the wind; one hears only that the inner treasury has spent millions of strings of cash and the Sacrificial Administration has ordained more than five thousand clerics.

sentences.zh: 以此爲術，其誰不能？

translations.literal: With this as a method, who cannot do it?
translations.idiomatic: Who cannot do this?

sentences.zh: 而所行之事，道路皆知其難。

translations.literal: Yet the things being done are known on every road to be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yet everyone knows how hard the policies being pursued really are.

sentences.zh: 汴水濁流，自生民以來，不以種稻。

translations.literal: The Bian River is a muddy stream; since the birth of the people, rice has not been planted in it.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian River runs muddy; since antiquity no one has grown rice in it.

sentences.zh: 今欲陂而清之，萬頃之稻，必用千頃之陂，一歲一淤，三歲而滿矣。

translations.literal: Now you wish to dam it and clear it; ten thousand mu of rice would require a thousand mu of reservoir, silting once a year and filling in three years.
translations.idiomatic: To dam and clear it for rice would require a vast reservoir that silts yearly and fills within three years.

sentences.zh: 陛下遂信其說，卽使相視地形，所在鑿空，訪尋水利，妄庸輕剽，率意爭言。

translations.literal: Your Majesty then believed this doctrine and at once sent men to survey the terrain, boring holes wherever they went, seeking waterworks; reckless mediocrities and light fops competed in speech at will.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed them and sent surveyors to bore holes everywhere in search of water projects, while reckless adventurers competed to offer schemes.

sentences.zh: 官司雖知其疏，不敢便行抑退，追集老少，相視可否。

translations.literal: Though officials knew the plans were flawed, they dared not promptly suppress and dismiss them; they gathered old and young to see whether things were feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Officials knew the plans were flawed but dared not reject them outright; they gathered locals to judge feasibility.

sentences.zh: 若非灼然難行，必須且爲興役。

translations.literal: Unless clearly impossible, they had to undertake the work for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Unless plainly unworkable, labor had to proceed.

sentences.zh: 官吏苟且順從，真謂陛下有意興作，上糜帑廩，下奪農時。

translations.literal: Officials perfunctorily complied, truly believing Your Majesty wished to undertake projects, wasting treasury stores above and seizing farmers' seasons below.
translations.idiomatic: Officials complied, believing the emperor truly wished to build, wasting treasury funds above and seizing the farming season below.

sentences.zh: 堤防一開，水失故道，雖食議者之肉，何補於民！

translations.literal: Once dikes are opened, water loses its old course; even if one ate the flesh of those who proposed it, what help would that be to the people!
translations.idiomatic: Once dikes are breached, the river loses its course; even punishing the planners would not help the people.

sentences.zh: 臣不知朝廷何苦而爲此哉？

translations.literal: Your subject does not know why the court troubles itself to do this.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know why the court insists on this.

sentences.zh: 自古役人，必用鄉戶。

translations.literal: Since antiquity corvée labor has employed local household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity corvée has relied on local household registers.

sentences.zh: 今者徒聞江、浙之間，數郡顧役，而欲措之天下。

translations.literal: Now one only hears that between the Yangzi and Zhejiang a few prefectures use hired service and yet wishes to impose this on the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: A few prefectures in Jiangsu and Zhejiang use hired service, yet you wish to impose this on the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 單丁、女戶，蓋天民之窮者也，而陛下首欲役之，富有四海，忍不加恤！

translations.literal: Single adult sons and female-headed households are among the poorest of Heaven's people, yet Your Majesty would first make them serve corvée; possessing all within the four seas, can you bear not to pity them!
translations.idiomatic: Single sons and female-headed households are the poorest subjects, yet you would conscript them first; ruling all under Heaven, can you not pity them?

sentences.zh: 自楊炎爲兩稅，租調與庸旣兼之矣，奈何復欲取庸？

translations.literal: Since Yang Yan established the two-tax system, rent, adjustment, and corvée service were already combined; why again wish to take corvée?
translations.idiomatic: Since Yang Yan's two-tax reform combined rent and corvée, why take corvée again?

sentences.zh: 萬一後世不幸有聚斂之臣，庸錢不除，差役仍舊，推所從來，則必有任其咎者矣。

translations.literal: If in later ages there should unhappily be a minister who gathers revenue, with corvée money not abolished and assigned service continuing as before, tracing whence it came, there will surely be one who bears the blame.
translations.idiomatic: If later ages bring a rapacious minister, with corvée payments retained and assigned service continuing, posterity will trace the blame to this reign.

sentences.zh: 青苗放錢，自昔有禁。

translations.literal: Green Sprouts loans were forbidden since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Lending grain at interest was forbidden in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 今陛下始立成法，每歲常行。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has for the first time established a standing law to carry it out every year.
translations.idiomatic: Now you have made it a permanent annual practice.

sentences.zh: 雖云不許抑配，而數世之後，暴君汙吏，陛下能保之與？

translations.literal: Though it is said forced allocation is not allowed, several generations hence can Your Majesty guarantee this against tyrants and corrupt officials?
translations.idiomatic: Though forced allocation is forbidden today, can you guarantee that tyrants and corrupt officials of later ages will obey?

sentences.zh: 計願請之戶，必皆孤貧不濟之人，鞭撻已急，則繼之逃亡，不還，則均及鄰保，勢有必至，異日天下恨之，國史記之，曰『青苗錢自陛下始』，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Those who must request loans will surely all be orphans and poor unable to support themselves; when the whip is already urgent, flight follows; if they do not repay, neighbors and mutual-aid groups are charged equally—the trend must reach this; someday the realm will hate it and the national history will record, "Green Sprouts money began with Your Majesty"—is this not to be regretted!
translations.idiomatic: Borrowers will be orphans and the destitute; when the lash falls they flee, and neighbors are held liable for their debts—posterity will record that Green Sprouts money began with your reign. Is that not lamentable?

sentences.zh: 且常平之法，可謂至矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Ever-Normal Granary system can be called perfect.
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Normal Granary system was already excellent.

sentences.zh: 今欲變爲青苗，壞彼成此，所喪逾多，虧官害民，雖悔何及！

translations.literal: Now you wish to change it into Green Sprouts, destroying the accomplished to create this; the loss exceeds the gain, harming the offices and injuring the people—even regret cannot avail!
translations.idiomatic: Replacing it with Green Sprouts destroys what worked; the loss exceeds the gain, harming both treasury and people beyond recall.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝以財力匱竭，用賈人桑羊之說，買賤賣貴，謂之均輸。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han, his finances exhausted, adopted the merchant Sang Hongyang's plan to buy cheap and sell dear, calling it Equitable Transport.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu's treasury was empty, he adopted Sang Hongyang's plan to buy cheap and sell dear, called Equitable Transport.

sentences.zh: 于時商賈不行，盜賊滋熾，幾至於亂。

translations.literal: At that time merchants did not travel and bandits flourished, nearly reaching disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants ceased trading, banditry flourished, and the realm nearly fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 孝昭旣立，霍光順民所欲而予之，天下歸心，遂以無事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhao succeeded, Huo Guang followed the people's wishes and restored it to them; the realm turned its hearts to him and thus was without incident.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhao succeeded, Huo Guang restored trade to the people; the realm turned to him and peace returned.

sentences.zh: 不意今日此論復興。

translations.literal: One did not expect this doctrine to rise again today.
translations.idiomatic: One did not expect this doctrine revived today.

sentences.zh: 立法之初，其費已厚，縱使薄有所獲，而徵商之額，所損必多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of legislation the costs were already heavy; even if there is slight gain, the amount lost in merchant taxes must be greater.
translations.idiomatic: The new laws were costly from the start; any slight gain is outweighed by losses in merchant taxes.

sentences.zh: 譬之有人爲其主畜牧，以一牛易五羊。

translations.literal: It is like a man who herds for his master and trades one ox for five sheep.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a herdsman who trades one of his master's oxen for five sheep.

sentences.zh: 一牛之失，則隱而不言；

translations.literal: The loss of one ox he conceals and does not speak of;
translations.idiomatic: He hides the loss of the ox and says nothing;

sentences.zh: 五羊之獲，則指爲勞績。

translations.literal: the gain of five sheep he points to as merit.
translations.idiomatic: but points to the five sheep as merit.

sentences.zh: 今壞常平而言青苗之功，虧商稅而取均輸之利，何以異此？

translations.literal: Now destroying Ever-Normal to speak of Green Sprouts' merit, losing merchant taxes to take Equitable Transport's profit—how is this different?
translations.idiomatic: Destroying Ever-Normal to praise Green Sprouts, losing merchant taxes for Equitable Transport—how is this different?

sentences.zh: 臣竊以爲過矣。

translations.literal: Your subject privately believes this is an error.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this is a mistake.

sentences.zh: 議者必謂：『民可與樂成，難與慮始。』

translations.literal: Those who debate will surely say, "The people can be made to rejoice in the completion but find it hard to deliberate the beginning."
translations.idiomatic: Critics will say, "The people rejoice in results but resist beginnings."

sentences.zh: 故陛下堅執不顧，期於必行。

translations.literal: Therefore Your Majesty firmly holds and does not look back, expecting it must be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore you persist, determined to enforce the laws.

sentences.zh: 此乃戰國貪功之人，行險僥倖之說，未及樂成，而怨已起矣。

translations.literal: This is the talk of men of the Warring States who coveted merit, practicing dangerous schemes for lucky gain; before rejoicing in completion, resentment has already arisen.
translations.idiomatic: This is the talk of Warring States adventurers seeking quick profit; resentment has arisen before any benefit.

sentences.zh: 臣之所願陛下結人心者，此也。

translations.literal: What your subject wishes in Your Majesty's binding the hearts of the people is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I mean by winning the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 國家之所以存亡者，在道德之淺深，不在乎強與弱；

translations.literal: What makes a state survive or perish is the depth or shallowness of moral power, not strength or weakness;
translations.idiomatic: Whether a state survives depends on moral depth, not strength;

sentences.zh: 歷數之所以長短者，在風俗之薄厚，不在乎富與貧。

translations.literal: what makes a dynasty long or short is the thickness or thinness of customs, not wealth or poverty.
translations.idiomatic: whether a dynasty endures depends on customs, not wealth.

sentences.zh: 人主知此，則知所輕重矣。

translations.literal: If the ruler knows this, then he knows what to value lightly or heavily.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler knows this, he knows what matters.

sentences.zh: 故臣願陛下務崇道德而厚風俗，不願陛下急於有功而貪富強。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject wishes Your Majesty to esteem moral power and enrich customs, not to hurry after achievement and covet wealth and strength.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to esteem morality and enrich customs, not to hurry after achievement and covet wealth and power.

sentences.zh: 愛惜風俗，如護元氣。

translations.literal: Cherish customs as one protects vital qi.
translations.idiomatic: Cherish customs as you would protect the body's vital breath.

sentences.zh: 聖人非不知深刻之法可以齊眾，勇悍之夫可以集事，忠厚近於迂闊，老成初若遲鈍。

translations.literal: Sages are not ignorant that severe laws can align the multitude or that fierce bold men can gather affairs; generous sincerity seems near to pedantry and seasoned experience at first seems slow and dull.
translations.idiomatic: Sages know that harsh laws can control the masses and fierce men can get things done; generosity seems pedantic and experience seems slow.

sentences.zh: 然終不肯以彼易此者，知其所得小，而所喪大也。

translations.literal: Yet in the end they are unwilling to exchange this for that, knowing that what is gained is small and what is lost is great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they refuse to trade the latter for the former, knowing the gain is small and the loss great.

sentences.zh: 仁祖持法至寬，用人有敘，專務掩覆過失，未嘗輕改舊章。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong held the law to the utmost breadth, employed men with order, devoted himself to covering faults, and never lightly changed old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was lenient in law, orderly in appointments, covered officials' faults, and rarely changed old rules.

sentences.zh: 考其成功，則曰未至。

translations.literal: Examining his achievement, one says it had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by results, his reign seemed incomplete.

sentences.zh: 以言乎用兵，則十出而九敗；

translations.literal: In speaking of employing troops, nine campaigns out of ten failed;
translations.idiomatic: In war, nine campaigns in ten failed;

sentences.zh: 以言乎府庫，則僅足而無餘。

translations.literal: in speaking of treasuries, there was barely enough and no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: the treasury was barely full.

sentences.zh: 徒以德澤在人，風俗知義，故升遐之日，天下歸仁焉。

translations.literal: Only because his moral grace was in the people and customs knew righteousness, on the day he ascended to the remote, the realm turned its benevolence to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his kindness lived in the people and customs held to righteousness, so when he died the realm mourned him with devotion.

sentences.zh: 議者見其末年吏多因循，事不振舉，乃欲矯之以苛察，齊之以智能，招來新進勇銳之人，以圖一切速成之效。

translations.literal: Those who debated, seeing that in his late years many officials were routine-bound and affairs were not vigorously pursued, wished to correct this with harsh scrutiny, align it with clever ability, and recruit new men who were bold and sharp to seek the effect of accomplishing all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Critics, seeing late Renzong officials as sluggish, wished to correct them with harsh scrutiny and recruit bold new men for quick results.

sentences.zh: 未享其利，澆風已成。

translations.literal: Before enjoying the benefit, a corrupting wind had already formed.
translations.idiomatic: Before any benefit appeared, a corrupting wind had already risen.

sentences.zh: 多開驟進之門，使有意外之得，公卿侍從跬步可圖，俾常調之人舉生非望，欲望風俗之厚，豈可得哉？

translations.literal: Opening many gates for sudden advancement so that unexpected gains are possible, high ministers and attendants attainable in a short step, making those of regular appointment all harbor improper hopes—can one desire customs to be thick?
translations.idiomatic: Opening paths to sudden advancement, making regular officials dream of quick promotion—can customs grow thick?

sentences.zh: 近歲樸拙之人愈少，巧進之士益多。

translations.literal: In recent years plain honest men grow fewer and clever climbers grow more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Plain honest men grow fewer and clever climbers more numerous.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下哀之救之，以簡易爲法，以清淨爲心，而民德歸厚。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty pities and saves them, taking simplicity as law and purity as heart, will the people's virtue return to thickness.
translations.idiomatic: Only if you pity them, take simplicity as law and purity as heart, will popular virtue thicken again.

sentences.zh: 臣之所願陛下厚風俗者，此也。

translations.literal: What your subject wishes in Your Majesty's enriching customs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I mean by enriching customs.

sentences.zh: 祖宗委任臺諫，未嘗罪一言者。

translations.literal: The ancestral emperors entrusted the remonstrance and censorial offices and never punished a single word.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral emperors entrusted the censorate and never punished a single remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 縱有薄責，旋卽超升，許以風聞，而無官長。

translations.literal: Even if there was slight censure, promotion quickly followed; they were allowed to report what they heard and had no official superior.
translations.idiomatic: Even slight censure was followed by quick promotion; they reported what they heard without a superior.

sentences.zh: 言及乘輿，則天子改容；

translations.literal: When speech touched the imperial carriage, the Son of Heaven changed expression;
translations.idiomatic: When speech touched the throne, the emperor changed expression;

sentences.zh: 事關廊廟，則宰相待罪。

translations.literal: when affairs concerned the court hall, the chief minister awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: when affairs concerned the court, the chief minister awaited punishment.

sentences.zh: 臺諫固未必皆賢，所言亦未必皆是。

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrators were not necessarily all worthy, nor was what they said necessarily all correct.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were not all worthy, nor were their words always right.

sentences.zh: 然須養其銳氣，而借之重權者，豈徒然哉？

translations.literal: Yet it was necessary to nourish their sharp spirit and lend them heavy authority—was this for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Yet their spirit had to be nourished and their authority upheld—was this for nothing?

sentences.zh: 將以折奸臣之萌也。

translations.literal: It was to break the sprouting of treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: It was to check treacherous ministers at the outset.

sentences.zh: 今法令嚴密，朝廷清明，所謂奸臣，萬無此理。

translations.literal: Now laws and orders are strict and the court is clear; so-called treacherous ministers have no such reason under ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Today laws are strict and the court is clear; treachery is scarcely possible.

sentences.zh: 然養貓以去鼠，不可以無鼠而養不捕之貓；

translations.literal: Yet one raises cats to catch mice and cannot, because there are no mice, raise cats that do not catch;
translations.idiomatic: One keeps cats to catch mice and cannot, for lack of mice, keep cats that do not hunt;

sentences.zh: 畜狗以防盜，不可以無盜而畜不吠之狗。

translations.literal: one keeps dogs to guard against thieves and cannot, because there are no thieves, keep dogs that do not bark.
translations.idiomatic: one keeps dogs to guard against thieves and cannot, for lack of thieves, keep dogs that do not bark.

sentences.zh: 陛下得不上念祖宗設此官之意，下爲子孫萬世之防？

translations.literal: Can Your Majesty fail to reflect above on the ancestral emperors' purpose in establishing these offices and below provide a safeguard for ten thousand generations of descendants?
translations.idiomatic: Will you not recall why the ancestral emperors created these offices and safeguard your descendants for ten thousand generations?

sentences.zh: 臣聞長老之談，皆謂臺諫所言，常隨天下公議。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard elders say that what censors and remonstrators speak often follows the public consensus of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Elders say that censors speak as public opinion directs.

sentences.zh: 公議所與，臺諫亦與之；

translations.literal: What public consensus approves, censors also approve;
translations.idiomatic: What the public approves, censors approve;

sentences.zh: 公議所擊，臺諫亦擊之。

translations.literal: what public consensus attacks, censors also attack.
translations.idiomatic: what the public condemns, censors condemn.

sentences.zh: 今者物論沸騰，怨讟交至，公議所在，亦知之矣。

translations.literal: Now popular discussion boils and resentment and slander arrive together; where public consensus lies, you also know it.
translations.idiomatic: Now popular discussion boils with resentment; you know where public consensus lies.

sentences.zh: 臣恐自茲以往，習慣成風，盡爲執政私人，以致人主孤立，紀綱一廢，何事不生！

translations.literal: Your subject fears that from now on, habit will become custom and all will become private retainers of those in power, causing the ruler to stand alone, institutions and standards to be abolished, and every kind of trouble to arise!
translations.idiomatic: I fear that hereafter censors will become partisans of the ruling faction, leaving the ruler isolated and institutions ruined.

sentences.zh: 臣之所願陛下存紀綱者，此也。」

translations.literal: What your subject wishes in Your Majesty's preserving institutions and standards is this."
translations.idiomatic: This is what I mean by preserving institutions."

sentences.zh: 軾見安石贊神宗以獨斷專任，因試進士發策，以「晉武平吳以獨斷而克，苻堅伐晉以獨斷而亡，齊恒專任管仲而霸，燕噲專任子之而敗，事同而功異」爲問，安石滋怒，使御史謝景溫論奏其過，窮治無所得，軾遂請外，通判杭州。

translations.literal: Shi saw that Anshi praised Shenzong for independent decision and sole appointment; therefore in examining Presented Scholars he set a policy question on "Jin Wu pacified Wu through independent decision and succeeded, Fu Jian attacked Jin through independent decision and perished; Duke Huan of Qi solely employed Guan Zhong and hegemonized, King Kuai of Yan solely employed Zi Zhi and was ruined—affairs the same but merit different," and Anshi grew angrier still. He had investigating censor Xie Jingwen memorialize his faults; though investigation found nothing, Shi thereupon requested an outside post and was made vice prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi saw Wang Anshi praise the emperor for acting alone, he set an examination question contrasting rulers who succeeded or failed through sole reliance on ministers. Wang Anshi was furious and had the censor Xie Jingwen investigate him. Finding no fault, Shi requested an outside post and was appointed vice prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高麗入貢，使者發幣於官吏，書稱甲子。

translations.literal: Koryo entered tribute; the envoy distributed gifts to officials, and the letter used the sexagenary cycle.
translations.idiomatic: When Koryo sent tribute, the envoy distributed gifts to officials in a letter dated by the sexagenary cycle alone.

sentences.zh: 軾卻之曰：「高麗於本朝稱臣，而不稟正朔，吾安敢受！」

translations.literal: Shi refused it, saying, "Koryo toward our dynasty calls itself subject but does not follow our calendar; how dare I accept!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi refused, saying, "Koryo calls itself our subject yet does not use our calendar—how dare I accept this?"

sentences.zh: 使者易書稱熙寧，然後受之。

translations.literal: The envoy changed the letter to read Xining, and only then did he accept.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy changed the letter to the Xining reign title, and only then did Shi accept.

sentences.zh: 時新政日下，軾於其間，每因法以便民，民賴以安。

translations.literal: At that time the new policies daily descended; amid them Shi often used the laws to benefit the people where convenient, and the people relied on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: As new policies poured forth, Shi often used them where possible to help the people, who were thereby spared hardship.

sentences.zh: 徙知密州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 司農行手實法，不時施行者以違制論。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Agriculture implemented the hand-verification law; those who did not carry it out on schedule were punished for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Agriculture enforced the hand-verification law; failure to implement it on schedule was punished as a regulatory violation.

sentences.zh: 軾謂提舉官曰：「違制之坐，若自朝廷，誰敢不從？

translations.literal: Shi said to the promoting official, "If the charge of violating regulations came from the court itself, who would dare not obey?
translations.idiomatic: Shi told the promoting official, "If this order came from the court itself, who would dare disobey?

sentences.zh: 今出於司農，是擅造律也。」

translations.literal: Now it comes from the Directorate of Agriculture—this is to usurp the making of laws."
translations.idiomatic: But it comes from the Directorate of Agriculture—that is to usurp lawmaking."

sentences.zh: 提舉官驚曰：「公姑徐之。」

translations.literal: The promoting official started and said, "Your Grace, please go slowly."
translations.idiomatic: The official was alarmed and said, "Please wait, Your Grace."

sentences.zh: 未幾，朝廷知法害民，罷之。

translations.literal: Before long the court learned the law harmed the people and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court learned the law harmed the people and abolished it.

sentences.zh: 有盜竊發，安撫司遣三班使臣領悍卒來捕，卒凶暴恣行，至以禁物誣民，入其家爭鬪殺人，且畏罪驚潰，將爲亂。

translations.literal: When banditry broke out, the Pacification Commission sent a third-rank envoy leading fierce soldiers to capture them; the soldiers were brutal and acted at will, even accusing common people with contraband, entering homes to fight and kill; moreover fearing guilt they panicked and fled, about to cause disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits appeared, the Pacification Commission sent fierce soldiers who brutalized the people, falsely accused them of contraband, killed them in their homes, then panicked and nearly caused a riot.

sentences.zh: 民奔訴軾，軾投其書不視，曰：「必不至此。」

translations.literal: The people ran to tell Shi; Shi threw down their petitions unread, saying, "It surely will not come to that."
translations.idiomatic: The people appealed to Shi; he threw down their petitions unread, saying, "It will not come to that."

sentences.zh: 散卒聞之，少安，徐使人招出戮之。

translations.literal: When the scattered soldiers heard this, they were somewhat reassured; he slowly sent men to summon them out and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers calmed somewhat; he then had them summoned out and executed.

sentences.zh: 徙知徐州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 河決曹村，泛於梁山泊，溢于南清河，匯于城下，漲不時洩，城將敗，富民爭出避水。

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke at Caocun, spread into Liangshan Marsh, overflowed the Southern Qing River, pooled below the city, rose without timely release, and the city was about to fall; the wealthy competed to flee the flood.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River broke at Caocun, flooded into Liangshan Marsh and the Southern Qing River, pooled below Xuzhou, and the city was about to fall; the wealthy fled.

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「富民出，民皆動搖，吾誰與守？

translations.literal: Shi said, "If the wealthy leave, the people will all be shaken—whom shall I defend it with?
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "If the wealthy flee, the people will panic—whom shall I defend the city with?

sentences.zh: 吾在是，水決不能敗城。」

translations.literal: As long as I am here, the water cannot defeat the city."
translations.idiomatic: While I remain, the flood cannot take the city."

sentences.zh: 驅使復入。

translations.literal: He drove them to return.
translations.idiomatic: He drove them back inside.

sentences.zh: 軾詣武衛營，呼卒長曰：「河將害城，事急矣，雖禁軍且爲我盡力。」

translations.literal: Shi went to the Martial Guards camp and called the squad leader, saying, "The river is about to harm the city; the matter is urgent—even the forbidden army must exert itself for me."
translations.idiomatic: Shi went to the Martial Guards camp and told the squad leader, "The river threatens the city; even the imperial guards must help."

sentences.zh: 卒長曰：「太守猶不避塗潦，吾儕小人，當效命。」

translations.literal: The squad leader said, "The prefect himself does not avoid the mud—how could we petty men not give our lives?"
translations.idiomatic: The leader replied, "The prefect does not shun the mud—how can we petty men not serve?"

sentences.zh: 率其徒持畚鍤以出，築東南長堤，首起戲馬臺，尾屬于城。

translations.literal: He led his men out with baskets and spades and built a long dike on the southeast, beginning at the Cockfighting Terrace and ending at the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: They built a long dike from the Cockfighting Terrace to the city wall.

sentences.zh: 雨日夜不止，城不沈者三版。

translations.literal: Rain fell day and night without cease; the city did not sink by three board-lengths.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell day and night; the city sank no more than three board-lengths.

sentences.zh: 軾廬於其上，過家不入，使官吏分堵以守，卒全其城。

translations.literal: Shi lodged on the dike, did not enter his home when passing it, had officials guard in sections, and the soldiers preserved the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: Shi lived on the dike, passed his home without entering, set officials to guard by section, and saved the city.

sentences.zh: 復請調來歲夫增築故城，爲木岸，以虞水之再至。

translations.literal: He again requested corvée from the coming year to heighten the old city wall and build a timber revetment against a second flood.
translations.idiomatic: He requested corvée the next year to heighten the old wall and build a timber revetment against future floods.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 徙知湖州，上表以謝。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Huzhou and submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Huzhou and submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 又以事不便民者不敢言，以詩託諷，庶有補於國。

translations.literal: Because he dared not speak of matters inconvenient to the people in prose, he entrusted remonstrance to poetry, hoping it might benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to speak openly of policies that harmed the people, he voiced his criticism in poetry, hoping to benefit the state.

sentences.zh: 御史李定、舒亶、何正臣摭其表語，並媒蘖所爲詩以爲訕謗，逮赴臺獄，欲置之死，鍛煉久之不決。

translations.literal: Investigating censors Li Ding, Shu Dan, and He Zhenchen seized phrases from his memorial and also fabricated charges from his poems as slander; he was arrested and sent to the prison of the Censorate, and they wished to put him to death, forging evidence for a long time without reaching a decision.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Li Ding, Shu Dan, and He Zhenchen twisted his memorial and poems into charges of slander; he was imprisoned and they sought his death, but prolonged interrogation brought no verdict.

sentences.zh: 神宗獨憐之，以黃州團練副使安置。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong alone pitied him and appointed him Vice Military Training Commissioner of Huangzhou for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong alone pitied him and appointed him Vice Military Training Commissioner of Huangzhou on probation.

sentences.zh: 軾與田父野老，相從溪山間，築室於東坡，自號「東坡居士」。

translations.literal: Shi kept company with farmers and old villagers of the countryside, roaming among streams and mountains; he built a dwelling at Dongpo and styled himself "Layman of Dongpo."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi lived among local farmers and villagers, wandering through streams and hills; he built a house at Dongpo and took the name "Dongpo Hermit."

sentences.zh: 三年，神宗數有意復用，輒爲當路者沮之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Emperor Shenzong several times intended to recall him to office, but each time those in power obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his exile, Emperor Shenzong repeatedly wanted to bring him back, but those in power blocked it each time.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘗語宰相王珪、蔡確曰：「國史至重，可命蘇軾成之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong once said to the chancellors Wang Gui and Cai Que: "The National History is of utmost importance; Su Shi could be ordered to complete it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong once told the chancellors Wang Gui and Cai Que, "The National History is far too important to neglect—we could assign Su Shi to complete it."

sentences.zh: 珪有難色。

translations.literal: Wang Gui showed a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui looked uneasy.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「軾不可，姑用曾鞏。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "Shi will not do; for the time being use Zeng Gong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Su Shi will not do; for now use Zeng Gong instead."

sentences.zh: 鞏進《太祖總論》，神宗意不允，遂手札移軾汝州，有曰：「蘇軾黜居思咎，閱歲滋深，人材實難，不忍終棄。」

translations.literal: Zeng Gong submitted his "General Discussion on Emperor Taizu," but the emperor was not satisfied; he then personally wrote a letter transferring Shi to Ruzhou, saying: "Su Shi, dwelling in dismissal and reflecting on his faults, has over the years grown ever deeper in repentance; talent is truly hard to find, and I cannot bear to abandon him utterly."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gong submitted his "General Discussion on Emperor Taizu," but the emperor was displeased; he then wrote personally to transfer Su Shi to Ruzhou, saying, "Su Shi, living in exile and reflecting on his faults, has grown ever deeper in repentance over the years. Talent is truly hard to find, and I cannot bear to cast him aside forever."

sentences.zh: 軾未至汝，上書自言饑寒，有田在常，願得居之。

translations.literal: Before Shi reached Ruzhou, he submitted a memorial stating his hunger and cold, saying he had land in Changzhou and wished to reside there.
translations.idiomatic: Before Su Shi reached Ruzhou, he petitioned the throne, saying he suffered hunger and cold and had land in Changzhou where he wished to live.

sentences.zh: 朝奏，夕報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized in the morning; by evening permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned in the morning; approval came that same evening.

sentences.zh: 道過金陵，見王安石，曰：「大兵大獄，漢、唐滅亡之兆。

translations.literal: Passing through Jinling on the way, he saw Wang Anshi and said: "Massive warfare and great judicial persecutions are portents of the fall of Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Jinling on his way, he met Wang Anshi and said, "Massive warfare and great judicial persecutions are the very signs by which Han and Tang fell.

sentences.zh: 祖宗以仁厚治天下，正欲革此。

translations.literal: Our ancestors governed the realm with benevolence and generosity, precisely to reform this.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding emperors governed the realm with benevolence and generosity precisely to root out such things.

sentences.zh: 今西方用兵，連年不解，東南數起大獄，公獨無一言以救之乎？」

translations.literal: Now the western campaigns drag on year after year without resolution, and in the southeast great prosecutions have repeatedly arisen—have you no word to save them?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the western campaigns drag on year after year without end, and in the southeast great prosecutions have repeatedly arisen—will you not speak a word to stop them?"

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「二事皆惠卿啓之，安石在外，安敢言？」

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Both matters were initiated by Huixin; Anshi is out of office—how would I dare speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi replied, "Both matters were Huixin's doing. I am out of office—how would I dare speak?"

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「在朝則言，在外則不言，事君之常禮耳。

translations.literal: Shi said: "When in court one speaks; when out of office one does not—such is the ordinary protocol of serving one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said, "When one is at court one speaks; when one is out of office one keeps silent—that is the ordinary way of serving one's sovereign.

sentences.zh: 上所以待公者，非常禮，公所以待上者，豈可以常禮乎？」

translations.literal: The way the sovereign treats you is not ordinary protocol; the way you treat the sovereign—can it be by ordinary protocol?"
translations.idiomatic: The way the sovereign has treated you is no ordinary courtesy. Can the way you treat the sovereign be governed by ordinary courtesy?"

sentences.zh: 安石厲聲曰：「安石須說。」

translations.literal: Anshi said sharply: "Anshi must speak."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said sharply, "I must speak."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「出在安石口，入在子瞻耳。」

translations.literal: He added: "It leaves Anshi's mouth and enters Zizhan's ear alone."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "What leaves my mouth enters your ears alone."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「人須是知行一不義，殺一不辜，得天下弗爲，乃可。」

translations.literal: He also said: "A man must know that he would not commit one injustice or kill one innocent person even to gain the realm—only then is he fit."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "A man must know that he would not commit one injustice or kill one innocent person even to gain the whole realm—only then is he fit."

sentences.zh: 軾戲曰：「今之君子，爭減半年磨勘，雖殺人亦爲之。」

translations.literal: Shi joked: "Today's gentlemen would commit murder for half a year's reduction in merit review."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi joked, "Today's gentlemen would commit murder for half a year off their merit review."

sentences.zh: 安石笑而不言。

translations.literal: Anshi laughed and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi laughed and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 至常，神宗崩，哲宗立，復朝奉郎、知登州，召爲禮部郎中。

translations.literal: When he reached Changzhou, Emperor Shenzong died and Emperor Zhezong ascended; he was restored to the post of Gentleman for Court Audience and made prefect of Dengzhou, then summoned as Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Changzhou, Emperor Shenzong died and Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne. Su Shi was restored to Gentleman for Court Audience and appointed prefect of Dengzhou, then summoned as Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 軾舊善司馬光、章惇。

translations.literal: Shi had long been on good terms with Sima Guang and Zhang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi had long been on good terms with Sima Guang and Zhang Dun.

sentences.zh: 時光爲門下侍郎，惇知樞密院，二人不相合，惇每以謔侮困光，光苦之。

translations.literal: At the time Guang was Vice Director of the Chancellery and Dun was Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; the two did not get along, and Dun often harassed Guang with mockery and insults, to Guang's distress.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sima Guang was Vice Director of the Chancellery and Zhang Dun was Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. The two did not get along, and Zhang Dun often mocked and humiliated Sima Guang, to his great distress.

sentences.zh: 軾謂惇曰：「司馬君卽時望甚重。

translations.literal: Shi said to Dun: "Master Sima already carries very great public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said to Zhang Dun, "Master Sima already enjoys immense public esteem.

sentences.zh: 昔許靖以虛名無實，見鄙於蜀先主，法正曰：『靖之浮譽，播流四海，若不加禮，必以賤賢爲累。』

translations.literal: Formerly Xu Jing, though empty of reputation and substance, was despised by the lord of Shu; Fa Zheng said: 'Jing's inflated reputation spreads throughout the four seas; if we fail to honor him, we shall surely be burdened by the charge of slighting worthies.'
translations.idiomatic: In the past Xu Jing, though all reputation and no substance, was looked down on by the lord of Shu. Fa Zheng said, "Jing's inflated fame has spread throughout the realm. If we fail to honor him, we shall surely be blamed for slighting the worthy."

sentences.zh: 先主納之，乃以靖爲司徒。

translations.literal: The lord of Shu accepted this and made Jing Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Shu accepted this and made Xu Jing Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 許靖且不可慢，況君實乎？」

translations.literal: If even Xu Jing could not be slighted, how much less Junshi?"
translations.idiomatic: If even Xu Jing could not be slighted, how much less Junshi?"

sentences.zh: 惇以爲然，光賴以少安。

translations.literal: Dun agreed, and Guang was thereby somewhat relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun agreed, and Sima Guang was somewhat relieved.

sentences.zh: 初，祖宗時，差役行久生弊，編戶充役者不習其役，又虐使之，多致破產，狹鄉民至有終歲不得息者。

translations.literal: In the beginning, during the reigns of the founding emperors, the corvée assignment system had long been in force and produced abuses; registered households assigned to labor service were unskilled in their duties and moreover were harshly driven, often ruining their families, and in narrow districts peasants sometimes went the whole year without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding emperors, the corvée assignment system had long been in force and had grown corrupt. Households drafted for labor were unskilled in their duties and were driven harshly, often ruining their families; in narrow districts peasants sometimes went the whole year without a day's rest.

sentences.zh: 王安石相神宗，改爲免役，使戶差高下出錢雇役，行法者過取，以爲民病。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi served as Shenzong's chancellor and changed it to the Service Substitution Tax, making households pay according to rank to hire labor; those enforcing the law took excessively, and this became a hardship for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi, serving as Shenzong's chancellor, replaced it with the Service Substitution Tax, requiring households to pay according to rank to hire laborers. Those enforcing the law overcharged, and this became a burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 司馬光爲相，知免役之害，不知其利，欲復差役，差官置局，軾與其選。

translations.literal: When Sima Guang became chancellor, he knew the harm of the Service Substitution Tax but not its benefits, and wished to restore corvée assignment; officials were dispatched to establish a bureau, and Shi was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang became chancellor, he saw the harm of the Service Substitution Tax but not its benefits, and wished to restore corvée assignment. Officials were dispatched to establish a bureau, and Su Shi was among those selected.

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「差役、免役，各有利害。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Corvée assignment and the Service Substitution Tax each have benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said, "Corvée assignment and the Service Substitution Tax each have benefits and harms.

sentences.zh: 免役之害，掊斂民財，十室九空，斂聚於上而下有錢荒之患。

translations.literal: The harm of the Service Substitution Tax is that it squeezes the people's wealth until nine of ten households are emptied, funds are gathered above while below there is a shortage of money.
translations.idiomatic: The harm of the Service Substitution Tax is that it squeezes the people's wealth until nine of ten households are ruined, money is gathered at the top while below there is a shortage of cash.

sentences.zh: 差役之害，民常在官，不得專力于農，而貪吏猾胥得緣爲奸。

translations.literal: The harm of corvée assignment is that the people are constantly tied to official service and cannot devote themselves fully to farming, while greedy clerks and wily subordinates find opportunities for misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: The harm of corvée assignment is that the people are constantly tied to official service and cannot devote themselves fully to farming, while greedy clerks and wily subordinates find openings for corruption.

sentences.zh: 此二害輕重，蓋略等矣。」

translations.literal: These two harms in weight are roughly equal."
translations.idiomatic: These two harms are roughly equal in severity."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「於君何如？」

translations.literal: Guang said: "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang asked, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「法相因則事易成，事有漸則民不驚。

translations.literal: Shi said: "When laws follow one upon another, affairs are easily accomplished; when matters proceed gradually, the people are not alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi replied, "When laws follow one upon another, affairs are easily accomplished; when change proceeds gradually, the people are not alarmed.

sentences.zh: 三代之法，兵農爲一，至秦始分爲二，及唐中葉，盡變府兵爲長徵之卒。

translations.literal: Under the law of the Three Dynasties, soldier and farmer were one; not until Qin were they divided into two; by the mid-Tang all garrison militia had been changed into long-service recruits.
translations.idiomatic: Under the law of the Three Dynasties, soldier and farmer were one; not until Qin were they divided; by the mid-Tang all garrison militia had been converted into long-service troops.

sentences.zh: 自爾以來，民不知兵，兵不知農，農出穀帛以養兵，兵出性命以衛農，天下便之。

translations.literal: Since then the people no longer knew warfare and soldiers no longer knew farming; farmers supplied grain and cloth to sustain soldiers, and soldiers gave their lives to protect farmers, and the realm found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Since then farmers no longer knew war and soldiers no longer knew farming. Farmers supplied grain and cloth to sustain the army; soldiers gave their lives to protect the farmers. The realm found this arrangement convenient.

sentences.zh: 雖聖人復起，不能易也。

translations.literal: Even if a sage arose again, he could not change it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if a sage arose again, he could not change it.

sentences.zh: 今免役之法，實大類此。

translations.literal: The present Service Substitution Tax law is in fact greatly similar to this.
translations.idiomatic: The present Service Substitution Tax is in fact very much like this.

sentences.zh: 公欲驟罷免役而行差役，正如罷長徵而復民兵，蓋未易也。」

translations.literal: You wish abruptly to abolish the Service Substitution Tax and restore corvée assignment—this is like abolishing long-service troops and reviving militia; I fear it would not be easy."
translations.idiomatic: You wish abruptly to abolish the Service Substitution Tax and restore corvée assignment. That is like abolishing long-service troops and reviving militia—it would not be easy."

sentences.zh: 光不以爲然。

translations.literal: Guang did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang did not agree.

sentences.zh: 軾又陳於政事堂，光忿然。

translations.literal: Shi stated his views again in the Hall of Administration, and Guang grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi stated his views again in the Hall of Administration, and Sima Guang grew angry.

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「昔韓魏公刺陝西義勇，公爲諫官，爭之甚力，韓公不樂，公亦不顧。

translations.literal: Shi said: "In the past when Duke Han of Wei dispatched voluntary troops in Shaanxi, you as remonstrance official argued against it with great force; Duke Han was displeased, yet you paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said, "In the past when Duke Han of Wei dispatched voluntary troops in Shaanxi, you as remonstrance official argued against it with great force. Duke Han was displeased, yet you paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 軾昔聞公道其詳，豈今日作相，不許軾盡言耶？」

translations.literal: I once heard you speak in detail of this—is it that today, as chancellor, you will not allow Shi to speak fully?"
translations.idiomatic: I once heard you speak in detail of this. Now that you are chancellor, will you not allow me to speak fully?"

sentences.zh: 光笑之。

translations.literal: Guang laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang laughed.

sentences.zh: 尋除翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the second year he additionally served as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
