translations.idiomatic: In the second year he additionally served as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 每進讀至治亂興衰、邪正得失之際，未嘗不反覆開導，覬有所啓悟。

translations.literal: Whenever he lectured and reached passages on the rise and fall of order and chaos, or the gains and losses of the orthodox and the deviant, he never failed to expound at length in the hope of awakening understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lectured and reached passages on the rise and fall of states, or the gains and losses of right and wrong, he never failed to expound at length, hoping to awaken understanding.

sentences.zh: 哲宗雖恭默不言，輒首肯之。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Zhezong remained respectfully silent and did not speak, he always nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Zhezong remained respectfully silent, he always nodded in assent.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀祖宗《寶訓》，因及時事，軾歷言：「今賞罰不明，善惡無所勸沮；

translations.literal: Once, reading the ancestral "Precious Instructions," he came to current affairs, and Shi enumerated: "Today rewards and punishments are unclear, and good and evil receive no encouragement or restraint;
translations.idiomatic: Once, reading the ancestral "Precious Instructions," he turned to current affairs, and Su Shi enumerated: "Today rewards and punishments are unclear, and good and evil receive no encouragement or restraint;

sentences.zh: 又黃河勢方北流，而強之使東；

translations.literal: moreover the Yellow River's current tends northward, yet we force it eastward;
translations.idiomatic: moreover the Yellow River's current tends northward, yet we force it eastward;

sentences.zh: 夏人入鎮戎，殺掠數萬人，帥臣不以聞。

translations.literal: the Tangut people entered Zhenrong, killing and plundering tens of thousands, yet the frontier commander did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: the Tanguts entered Zhenrong, killing and plundering tens of thousands, yet the frontier commander did not report it.

sentences.zh: 每事如此，恐浸成衰亂之漸。」

translations.literal: With each matter like this, I fear we are gradually forming the beginnings of decline and disorder."
translations.idiomatic: With each matter like this, I fear we are gradually sliding toward decline and disorder."

sentences.zh: 軾嘗鎖宿禁中，召入對便殿，宣仁后問曰：「卿前年爲何官？」

translations.literal: Shi once kept overnight vigil in the palace and was summoned to audience in the side hall; Empress Xuanren asked: "What office did you hold the year before last?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi once kept overnight vigil in the palace and was summoned to audience in the side hall. Empress Xuanren asked, "What office did you hold the year before last?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣爲常州團練副使。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject was Vice Military Training Commissioner of Changzhou."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your subject was Vice Military Training Commissioner of Changzhou."

sentences.zh: 曰：「今爲何官？」

translations.literal: She said: "What office do you hold now?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked, "What office do you hold now?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣今待罪翰林學士。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject now holds the post of Hanlin Academician in disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your subject now holds the post of Hanlin Academician, bearing disgrace."

sentences.zh: 曰：「何以遽至此？」

translations.literal: She said: "How did you reach this so quickly?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked, "How did you rise to this so quickly?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「遭遇太皇太后、皇帝陛下。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Through the grace of the Grand Empress Dowager and His Majesty the Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Through the grace of the Grand Empress Dowager and His Majesty the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 曰：「非也。」

translations.literal: She said: "That is not so."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "That is not so."

sentences.zh: 曰：「豈大臣論薦乎？」

translations.literal: He said: "Was it through recommendation by great ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "Was it through recommendation by great ministers?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「亦非也。」

translations.literal: She said: "That also is not so."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "That also is not so."

sentences.zh: 軾驚曰：「臣雖無狀，不敢自他途以進。」

translations.literal: Shi said in alarm: "Though your subject is unworthy, I dare not advance by any other path."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said in alarm, "Though I am unworthy, I dare not advance by any other path."

sentences.zh: 曰：「此先帝意也。

translations.literal: She said: "This was the former emperor's intention.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "This was the former emperor's intention.

sentences.zh: 先帝每誦卿文章，必歎曰：『奇才，奇才！』

translations.literal: Whenever the former emperor recited your writings, he always sighed and said: 'A prodigy—a prodigy!'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the former emperor recited your writings, he always sighed and said, "A prodigy—a prodigy!"

sentences.zh: 但未及進用卿耳。」

translations.literal: Only he did not live to employ you."
translations.idiomatic: Only he did not live to employ you."

sentences.zh: 軾不覺哭失聲，宣仁后與哲宗亦泣，左右皆感涕。

translations.literal: Shi involuntarily burst into sobs; Empress Xuanren and Emperor Zhezong wept as well, and all those present were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi involuntarily burst into sobs. Empress Xuanren and Emperor Zhezong wept as well, and all those present were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 已而命坐賜茶，徹御前金蓮燭送歸院。

translations.literal: Presently he was ordered to sit and was granted tea; the imperial golden lotus candles were carried out to escort him back to the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Presently he was invited to sit and granted tea; the imperial golden lotus candles were carried out to escort him back to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三年，權知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year he served as acting supervisor of the Ministry of Rites examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served as acting supervisor of the Ministry of Rites examinations.

sentences.zh: 會大雪苦寒，士坐庭中，噤未能言。

translations.literal: There happened to be great snow and bitter cold; the candidates sat in the courtyard, teeth chattering and unable to speak.
translations.idiomatic: There happened to be heavy snow and bitter cold. The candidates sat in the courtyard, teeth chattering and unable to speak.

sentences.zh: 軾寬其禁約，使得盡技。

translations.literal: Shi relaxed the prohibitions so they could display their full ability.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi relaxed the restrictions so they could display their full ability.

sentences.zh: 巡鋪內侍每摧辱舉子，且持曖昧單詞，誣以爲罪，軾盡奏逐之。

translations.literal: Internal attendants on patrol often humiliated examinees and, holding up ambiguous single words, falsely charged them with offenses; Shi memorialized to have them all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs on patrol often humiliated examinees and, seizing on ambiguous single words, falsely charged them with offenses. Su Shi memorialized to have them all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 四年，積以論事，爲當軸者所恨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, having repeatedly spoken out on state affairs, he was hated by those wielding power.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, having repeatedly spoken out on state affairs, he was hated by those in power.

sentences.zh: 軾恐不見容，請外，拜龍圖閣學士、知杭州。

translations.literal: Fearing he would not be tolerated, Shi requested an outside post and was appointed Hanlin Gentleman of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would not be tolerated, Su Shi requested an outside post and was appointed Hanlin Gentleman of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，諫官言前相蔡確知安州，作詩借郝處俊事以譏太皇太后。

translations.literal: Before he departed, remonstrance officials reported that the former chancellor Cai Que, as prefect of Anzhou, had composed poetry using the affair of Hao Chujun to mock the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, remonstrance officials reported that the former chancellor Cai Que, as prefect of Anzhou, had composed poetry alluding to Hao Chujun to mock the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 大臣議遷之嶺南。

translations.literal: The great ministers deliberated on banishing him to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers deliberated on banishing him to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 軾密疏：「朝廷若薄確之罪，則于皇帝孝治爲不足；

translations.literal: Shi submitted a secret memorial: "If the court treats Que's offense lightly, it will fall short of the emperor's filial governance;
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi submitted a secret memorial: "If the court treats Que's offense lightly, it will fall short of the emperor's filial governance;

sentences.zh: 若深罪確，則于太皇太后仁政爲小累。

translations.literal: if it punishes Que severely, it will be a slight burden on the Grand Empress Dowager's benevolent rule.
translations.idiomatic: if it punishes Que severely, it will be a slight stain on the Grand Empress Dowager's benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 謂宜皇帝敕置獄逮治，太皇太后出手詔赦之，則於仁孝兩得矣。」

translations.literal: I propose that His Majesty decree arrest and trial, and the Grand Empress Dowager issue a personal edict pardoning him—thus both benevolence and filial piety would be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that His Majesty decree arrest and trial, and the Grand Empress Dowager issue a personal edict pardoning him—thus both benevolence and filial piety would be satisfied."

sentences.zh: 宣仁后心善軾言而不能用。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanren approved Shi's words in her heart but could not adopt them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanren approved Su Shi's words in her heart but could not adopt them.

sentences.zh: 軾出郊，用前執政恩例，遣內侍賜龍茶、銀合，慰勞甚厚。

translations.literal: When Shi went out to the suburbs to take leave, the precedent for former chief administrators was applied and an internal attendant was sent to bestow dragon tea and a silver casket, with generous consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi went out to the suburbs to take leave, the precedent for former chief administrators was applied: an internal attendant was sent to bestow dragon tea and a silver casket, with generous words of consolation.

sentences.zh: 旣至杭，大旱，饑疫並作。

translations.literal: Once he reached Hangzhou, great drought struck and famine and pestilence arose together.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Hangzhou, severe drought struck and famine and pestilence arose together.

sentences.zh: 軾請於朝，免本路上供米三之一，復得賜度僧牒，易米以救饑者。

translations.literal: Shi petitioned the court to exempt one-third of the tribute grain supplied by his circuit, and also obtained permission to sell ordination certificates, exchanging them for grain to relieve the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi petitioned the court to exempt one-third of the tribute grain supplied by his circuit, and also obtained permission to sell ordination certificates, exchanging them for grain to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 明年春，又減價糶常平米，多作饘粥藥劑，遣使挾醫分坊治病，活者甚眾。

translations.literal: The following spring he again sold grain from the Ever-Normal Granary at reduced prices, prepared much gruel, porridge, and medicine, and sent agents with physicians to treat the sick ward by ward—very many lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he again sold grain from the Ever-Normal Granary at reduced prices, prepared large quantities of gruel, porridge, and medicine, and sent agents with physicians to treat the sick ward by ward. Very many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「杭，水陸之會，疫死比他處常多。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "Hangzhou is a meeting point of waterways and roads; deaths from pestilence are usually greater here than elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said, "Hangzhou is a crossroads of waterways and roads; deaths from pestilence are usually greater here than elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 乃裒羨緡得二千，復發橐中黃金五十兩，以作病坊，稍畜錢糧待之。

translations.literal: He therefore collected surplus funds totaling two thousand strings of cash, and also took fifty taels of gold from his own purse to build sick wards and set aside money and grain in reserve.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore collected surplus funds totaling two thousand strings of cash, and also took fifty taels of gold from his own purse to build sick wards and set aside money and grain in reserve.

sentences.zh: 杭本近海，地泉鹹苦，居民稀少。

translations.literal: Hangzhou originally lay near the sea; its groundwater was brackish and bitter, and residents were sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou originally lay near the sea. Its groundwater was brackish and bitter, and residents were sparse.

sentences.zh: 唐刺史李泌始引西湖水作六井，民足于水。

translations.literal: During the Tang, Prefect Li Bi first drew West Lake water to create six wells, and the people had enough water.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tang, Prefect Li Bi first drew West Lake water to create six wells, and the people had enough water.

sentences.zh: 白居易又浚西湖水入漕河，自河入田，所溉至千頃，民以殷富。

translations.literal: Bai Juyi further dredged West Lake water into the canal, and from the canal into the fields, irrigating up to a thousand qing; the people grew prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Juyi further dredged West Lake water into the canal and from the canal into the fields, irrigating up to a thousand qing. The people grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 湖水多葑，自唐及錢氏，歲輒浚治，宋興，廢之，葑積爲田，水無幾矣。

translations.literal: Duckweed filled much of the lake; from the Tang through the Qian clan, it was dredged every year, but after the Song rose this was abandoned, duckweed accumulated into fields, and little water remained.
translations.idiomatic: Duckweed filled much of the lake. From the Tang through the Qian clan it was dredged every year, but after the Song rose this was abandoned; duckweed accumulated into fields, and little water remained.

sentences.zh: 漕河失利，取給江潮，舟行市中，潮又多淤，三年一淘，爲民大患，六井亦幾於廢。

translations.literal: The canal lost its function and had to rely on river tides; boats sailed through the market district, yet the tides also silted heavily and required dredging every three years—a great affliction for the people—and the six wells were nearly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The canal lost its function and had to rely on river tides. Boats sailed through the market district, yet the tides also silted heavily and required dredging every three years—a great affliction for the people—and the six wells were nearly abandoned.

sentences.zh: 軾見茅山一河專受江潮，鹽橋一河專受湖水，遂浚二河以通漕。

translations.literal: Shi saw that one Mao Mountain canal received river tides exclusively and one Salt Bridge canal received lake water exclusively; he dredged both canals to restore transport.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi saw that one Mao Mountain canal received river tides exclusively and one Salt Bridge canal received lake water exclusively. He dredged both canals to restore transport.

sentences.zh: 復造堰閘，以爲湖水畜洩之限，江潮不復入市。

translations.literal: He also built weirs and sluice gates to regulate the storing and releasing of lake water, so that river tides no longer entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He also built weirs and sluice gates to regulate the storing and releasing of lake water, so that river tides no longer entered the city.

sentences.zh: 以餘力復完六井，又取葑田積湖中，南北徑三十里，爲長堤以通行者。

translations.literal: With remaining labor he restored the six wells, and also took the duckweed fields accumulated in the lake and made a long causeway thirty li from north to south for travelers.
translations.idiomatic: With remaining labor he restored the six wells, and also took the duckweed fields accumulated in the lake and built a long causeway thirty li from north to south for travelers.

sentences.zh: 吳人種菱，春輒芟除，不遣寸草。

translations.literal: People of Wu when growing water chestnuts clear them each spring, leaving not an inch of grass.
translations.idiomatic: People of Wu, when growing water chestnuts, clear them each spring, leaving not an inch of grass.

sentences.zh: 且募人種菱湖中，葑不復生。

translations.literal: He moreover hired people to grow water chestnuts in the lake, so duckweed no longer grew.
translations.idiomatic: He moreover hired people to grow water chestnuts in the lake, so duckweed no longer grew.

sentences.zh: 收其利以備脩湖，取救荒餘錢萬緡、糧萬石，及請得百僧度牒以募役者。

translations.literal: The profits were collected to fund lake maintenance; he took ten thousand strings of cash and ten thousand shi of grain left from famine relief, and also obtained a hundred ordination certificates to hire laborers.
translations.idiomatic: The profits were collected to fund lake maintenance. He took ten thousand strings of cash and ten thousand shi of grain left from famine relief, and also obtained a hundred ordination certificates to hire laborers.

sentences.zh: 堤成，植芙蓉、楊柳其上，望之如畫圖，杭人名爲蘇公堤。

translations.literal: When the causeway was complete, hibiscus and willows were planted upon it; viewed from afar it resembled a painted scroll, and the people of Hangzhou named it Su Causeway.
translations.idiomatic: When the causeway was complete, hibiscus and willows were planted upon it. Viewed from afar it resembled a painted scroll, and the people of Hangzhou named it Su Causeway.

sentences.zh: 杭僧淨源，舊居海濱，與舶客交通，舶至高麗，交譽之。

translations.literal: The Hangzhou monk Jingyuan had formerly lived on the seashore and associated with merchant voyagers; when the ships reached Goryeo, they all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Hangzhou monk Jingyuan had formerly lived on the seashore and associated with merchant voyagers. When the ships reached Goryeo, they all praised him.

sentences.zh: 元豐末，其王子義天來朝，因往拜焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanfeng era, that country's prince Yi Tian came to court and went to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanfeng era, Goryeo's Prince Uicheon came to court and went to pay his respects to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 至是，淨源死，其徒竊持其像，附舶往告。

translations.literal: By then Jingyuan had died; his disciples secretly took his image and went by ship to report it.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jingyuan had died; his disciples secretly took his image aboard a ship to deliver the news.

sentences.zh: 義天亦使其徒來祭，因持其國母二金塔，云祝兩宮壽。

translations.literal: Yi Tian also sent his disciples to make offerings, and brought two golden pagodas from his kingdom's queen mother, saying they were to pray for the longevity of the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Uicheon also sent disciples to make offerings, bearing two golden pagodas from his kingdom's queen mother, saying they were to pray for the longevity of the two palaces.

sentences.zh: 軾不納，奏之曰：「高麗久不入貢，失賜予厚利，意欲求朝，未測吾所以待之厚薄，故因祭亡僧而行祝壽之禮。

translations.literal: Shi did not accept them and memorialized, saying: "Goryeo has long ceased sending tribute and lost the great benefits of imperial gifts; they wish to seek an audience but cannot gauge how generously we will receive them, so they use this memorial for a dead monk to perform a longevity blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi refused to accept them and memorialized the throne: "Goryeo has long ceased sending tribute and lost the rich benefits of imperial gifts. They wish to seek an audience but cannot gauge how generously we will receive them, so they use this memorial service for a dead monk to perform a longevity blessing.

sentences.zh: 若受而不答，將生怨心；

translations.literal: If we accept without responding, resentment will arise;
translations.idiomatic: If we accept without responding, they will harbor resentment;

sentences.zh: 受而厚賜之，正墮其計。

translations.literal: if we accept and richly reward them, we fall right into their scheme.
translations.idiomatic: if we accept and richly reward them, we fall right into their scheme.

sentences.zh: 今宜勿與知，從州郡自以理卻之。

translations.literal: For now the court should not let them know our reasoning; let the prefectures and districts reject them on their own grounds.
translations.idiomatic: For now the court should not let them know our reasoning; let the prefectures and districts reject them on their own grounds.

sentences.zh: 彼庸僧猾商，爲國生事，漸不可長，宜痛加懲創。」

translations.literal: Those mediocre monks and cunning merchants stir up trouble for the state; this abuse must not be allowed to grow—they should be severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Such mediocre monks and cunning merchants stir up trouble for the state; this abuse must not be allowed to grow—they should be severely punished.

sentences.zh: 朝廷皆從之。

translations.literal: The court fully approved his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court fully approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，貢使果至，舊例，使所至吳越七州，費二萬四千餘緡。

translations.literal: Before long the tribute mission did arrive; under the old practice, wherever the envoys passed through the seven Wu-Yue prefectures, the cost exceeded twenty-four thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the tribute mission did arrive. Under the old practice, wherever the envoys passed through the seven Wu-Yue prefectures, the cost exceeded twenty-four thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 軾乃令諸州量事裁損，民獲交易之利，無復侵撓之害矣。

translations.literal: Shi then ordered the prefectures to trim expenses as circumstances allowed; the people gained the benefit of trade and were no longer harmed by harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi then ordered the prefectures to trim expenses as circumstances allowed. The people gained the benefit of trade and were no longer harmed by harassment.

sentences.zh: 浙江潮自海門東來，勢如雷霆，而浮山峙于江中，與漁浦諸山犬牙相錯，洄洑激射，歲敗公私船不可勝計。

translations.literal: The Qiantang River tide comes from the sea gate in the east with force like thunder; Fushan stands in mid-river, its contours interlocking with the hills of Yǔpǔ in jagged teeth; eddies surge and shoot forth, and each year public and private ships lost are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiantang River tide rolls in from the sea gate in the east with force like thunder. Fushan stands in mid-river, its contours interlocking with the hills of Yǔpǔ in jagged teeth; eddies surge and shoot forth, and each year public and private ships lost are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 軾議自浙江上流地名石門，並山而東，鑿爲漕河，引浙江及溪谷諸水二十餘里以達于江。

translations.literal: Shi proposed starting from Shimen, a place name upstream on the Qiantang River, cutting eastward along the mountains to carve a canal, drawing the Qiantang and various stream waters for more than twenty li to reach the river.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi proposed starting from Shimen, a place name upstream on the Qiantang River, cutting eastward along the mountains to carve a canal and drawing the Qiantang and various stream waters for more than twenty li to reach the river.

sentences.zh: 又並山爲岸，不能十里以達龍山大慈浦，自浦北折抵小嶺，鑿嶺六十五丈以達嶺東古河，浚古河數里達于龍山漕河，以避浮山之險，人以爲便。

translations.literal: Further, building banks along the mountains for less than ten li to reach Longshan Daci Ford, then turning north from the ford to reach Little Ridge, cutting through the ridge for sixty-five zhang to reach the ancient river east of the ridge, dredging the ancient river for several li to reach the Longshan canal—thus avoiding the danger of Fushan; people thought it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Further, building banks along the mountains for less than ten li to reach Longshan Daci Ford, then turning north from the ford to reach Little Ridge, cutting through the ridge for sixty-five zhang to reach the ancient river east of the ridge, and dredging the ancient river for several li to reach the Longshan canal—thus avoiding the danger of Fushan. People thought it convenient.

sentences.zh: 奏聞，有惡軾者，力沮之，功以故不成。

translations.literal: When he memorialized the throne, those who hated Shi forcefully obstructed the plan, and the work therefore was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: When he memorialized the throne, those who hated Su Shi forcefully obstructed the plan, and the work therefore was not completed.

sentences.zh: 軾復言：「三吳之水，瀦爲太湖，太湖之水，溢爲松江以入海。

translations.literal: Shi further said: "The waters of the Three Wu regions accumulate into Tai Lake; the waters of Tai Lake overflow into the Song River to reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi further said: "The waters of the Three Wu regions accumulate into Tai Lake; the waters of Tai Lake overflow into the Song River to reach the sea.

sentences.zh: 海日兩潮，潮濁而江清，潮水常欲淤塞江路，而江水清駛，隨輒滌去，海口常通，則吳中少水患。

translations.literal: The sea sends two tides daily; the tide is turbid and the river clear; the tide constantly seeks to silt up the river route, but the clear, swift river water washes it away, keeping the river mouth open—then central Wu has fewer flood disasters.
translations.idiomatic: The sea sends two tides daily. The tide is turbid and the river clear; the tide constantly seeks to silt up the river route, but the clear, swift river water washes it away and keeps the river mouth open—then central Wu has fewer flood disasters.

sentences.zh: 昔蘇州以東，公私船皆以篙行，無陸挽者。

translations.literal: Formerly east of Suzhou, public and private boats all traveled by pole and had no land haulage.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly east of Suzhou, public and private boats all traveled by pole and had no land haulage.

sentences.zh: 自慶曆以來，松江大築挽路，建長橋以扼塞江路，故今三吳多水，欲鑿挽路、爲十橋，以迅江勢」。

translations.literal: Since the Qingli era, massive haul roads were built on the Song River and long bridges erected to choke the river route, so now the Three Wu have much flooding; I wish to cut through the haul roads and build ten bridges to quicken the river's flow."
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qingli era, massive haul roads were built on the Song River and long bridges erected to choke the river route, so now the Three Wu have much flooding. I wish to cut through the haul roads and build ten bridges to quicken the river's flow."

sentences.zh: 亦不果用，人皆以爲恨。

translations.literal: This too was not adopted; people all regarded it as a regret.
translations.idiomatic: This too was not adopted, and people all regarded it as a regret.

sentences.zh: 軾二十年間再蒞杭，有德於民，家有畫像，飲食必祝。

translations.literal: Over twenty years Shi twice presided over Hangzhou and had virtue for the people; households kept his portrait and always blessed him at meals.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty years Su Shi twice presided over Hangzhou and had earned the people's gratitude; households kept his portrait and always blessed him at meals.

sentences.zh: 又作生祠以報。

translations.literal: They also built living shrines in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: They also built living shrines in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 六年，召爲吏部尚書，未至。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Minister of Personnel but had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was summoned as Minister of Personnel but had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 以弟轍除右丞，改翰林承旨。

translations.literal: Because his brother Zhe was appointed Right Vice Grand Councillor, he was changed to Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Because his brother Zhe was appointed Right Vice Grand Councillor, Su Shi was reassigned as Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 轍辭右丞，欲與兄同備從官，不聽。

translations.literal: Zhe declined the vice councillorship, wishing to serve alongside his brother as attendant officials; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe declined the vice councillorship, wishing to serve alongside his brother as attendant officials, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 軾在翰林數月，復以讒請外，乃以龍圖閣學士出知潁州。

translations.literal: Shi was in the Hanlin for several months, then again, because of slander, requested an outside post; he was sent out as Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall to govern Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi was in the Hanlin for several months, then again, because of slander, requested an outside post. He was sent out as Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall to govern Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，開封諸縣多水患，吏不究本末，決其陂澤，注之惠民河，河不能勝，致陳亦多水。

translations.literal: Previously the counties of Kaifeng had many flood disasters; officials did not investigate root causes and released their reservoirs and marshes into the Huimin River; the river could not bear it, causing Chen prefecture also to have much flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the counties of Kaifeng had many flood disasters. Officials did not investigate root causes and released their reservoirs and marshes into the Huimin River; the river could not bear it, causing Chen prefecture also to suffer much flooding.

sentences.zh: 又將鑿鄧艾溝與潁河並，且鑿黃堆欲注之於淮。

translations.literal: They were also going to dig Deng Ai's canal to join the Ying River, and dig Huangdui to pour into the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: They were also going to dig Deng Ai's canal to join the Ying River, and dig Huangdui to pour into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 軾始至潁，遣吏以水平準之，淮之漲水高於新溝幾一丈，若鑿黃堆，淮水顧流潁地爲患。

translations.literal: When Shi first reached Ying, he sent officials with a water level; the Huai's floodwater was nearly one zhang higher than the new ditch; if Huangdui were dug, Huai water would run back into Ying territory and become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi first reached Ying, he sent officials with a water level. The Huai's floodwater was nearly one zhang higher than the new ditch; if Huangdui were dug, Huai water would run back into Ying territory and become a disaster.

sentences.zh: 軾言於朝，從之。

translations.literal: Shi spoke to the court and his advice was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi spoke to the court and his advice was followed.

sentences.zh: 郡有宿賊尹遇等，數劫殺人，又殺捕盜吏兵。

translations.literal: The prefecture had hardened bandits such as Yin Yu, who repeatedly robbed and killed and also killed officers and soldiers sent to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had hardened bandits such as Yin Yu, who repeatedly robbed and killed and also killed officers and soldiers sent to capture them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以名捕不獲，被殺家復懼其害，匿不敢言。

translations.literal: The court issued warrants by name but could not capture them; families of the slain also feared further harm and hid and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued warrants by name but could not capture them. Families of the slain also feared further harm and hid, daring not speak.

sentences.zh: 軾召汝陰尉李直方曰：「君能禽此，當力言於朝，乞行優賞；

translations.literal: Shi summoned Ruyin Assistant Prefect Li Zhifang and said: "If you can capture these men, I shall strongly plead to the court for outstanding reward;
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi summoned Ruyin Assistant Prefect Li Zhifang and said: "If you can capture these men, I shall strongly plead to the court for outstanding reward;

sentences.zh: 不獲，亦以不職奏免君矣。」

translations.literal: if you fail, I shall also memorialize your dismissal for dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: if you fail, I shall also memorialize your dismissal for dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 直方有母且老，與母訣而後行。

translations.literal: Zhifang had an aged mother; he bade her farewell and then set out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang had an aged mother; he bade her farewell and then set out.

sentences.zh: 乃緝知盜所，分捕其黨與，手戟刺遇，獲之。

translations.literal: He then traced the bandits' whereabouts, divided forces to capture their accomplices, and personally stabbed Yin Yu with a halberd and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: He then traced the bandits' whereabouts, divided forces to capture their accomplices, and personally stabbed Yin Yu with a halberd and seized him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以小不應格，推賞不及。

translations.literal: The court held the case too minor to meet the standard and no reward was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court held the case too minor to meet the standard and no reward was granted.

sentences.zh: 軾請以己之年勞，當改朝散郎階，爲直方賞，不從。

translations.literal: Shi requested to use his own annual merit, due for promotion to Gentleman for Attendant Service, as Zhifang's reward; this was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi requested to use his own annual merit, due for promotion to Gentleman for Attendant Service, as Zhifang's reward, but this was denied.

sentences.zh: 其後吏部爲軾當遷，以符會其考，軾謂已許直方，又不報。

translations.literal: Later the Ministry of Personnel scheduled Shi's promotion according to his evaluation; Shi said he had already promised Zhifang and again received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Ministry of Personnel scheduled Su Shi's promotion according to his evaluation. Su Shi said he had already promised Zhifang and again received no response.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙揚州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊發運司主東南漕法，聽操舟者私載物貨，徵商不得留難。

translations.literal: Formerly the Transport Commission governed Southeast canal law, allowing boatmen to carry private goods; tax collectors could not obstruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Transport Commission governed Southeast canal law, allowing boatmen to carry private goods; tax collectors could not obstruct them.

sentences.zh: 故操舟者輒富厚，以官舟爲家，補其敝漏，且周船夫之乏，故所載率皆速達無虞。

translations.literal: Therefore boatmen grew wealthy, treating official boats as home, repairing their wear and leaks and also supplying boatmen's needs; thus cargoes mostly arrived swiftly without mishap.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore boatmen grew wealthy, treating official boats as home, repairing their wear and leaks and also supplying boatmen's needs. Thus cargoes mostly arrived swiftly without mishap.

sentences.zh: 近歲一切禁而不許，故舟弊人困，多盜所載以濟饑寒，公私皆病。

translations.literal: In recent years all was forbidden and not permitted; boats fell into disrepair and men were destitute; many stole what they carried to relieve hunger and cold—both public and private suffered.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years all was forbidden and not permitted. Boats fell into disrepair and men were destitute; many stole what they carried to relieve hunger and cold, and both public and private interests suffered.

sentences.zh: 軾請復舊，從之。

translations.literal: Shi requested restoration of the old practice; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi requested restoration of the old practice, and it was approved.

sentences.zh: 未閱歲，以兵部尚書召兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed he was summoned as Minister of War with concurrent appointment as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed he was summoned as Minister of War with concurrent appointment as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 是歲，哲宗親祀南郊，軾爲鹵簿使，導駕入太廟。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Zhezong personally performed the southern suburb sacrifice; Shi served as Master of the Guard of Honor, guiding the imperial procession into the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Zhezong personally performed the southern suburb sacrifice. Su Shi served as Master of the Guard of Honor, guiding the imperial procession into the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 有赭繖犢車並青蓋犢車十餘爭道，不避儀仗。

translations.literal: More than ten red-canopied calf carts and blue-canopied calf carts disputed the route, not yielding to the ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten red-canopied calf carts and blue-canopied calf carts disputed the route, not yielding to the ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 軾使御營巡檢使問之，乃皇后及大長公主。

translations.literal: Shi sent the Imperial Camp Inspector to inquire; they were the empress and the Grand Elder Princess.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi sent the Imperial Camp Inspector to inquire; they were the empress and the Grand Elder Princess.

sentences.zh: 時御史中丞李之純爲儀仗使，軾曰：「中丞職當肅政，不可不以聞之。」

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Li Zhichun was Master of Ceremonial Arms; Shi said: "The Censor-in-Chief's duty is to enforce discipline; this cannot go unreported.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief Li Zhichun was Master of Ceremonial Arms. Su Shi said: "The Censor-in-Chief's duty is to enforce discipline; this cannot go unreported.

sentences.zh: 純不敢言，軾于車中奏之。

translations.literal: Li Zhichun dared not speak; Shi memorialized from within his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhichun dared not speak; Su Shi memorialized from within his carriage.

sentences.zh: 哲宗遣使齎疏馳白太皇太后，明日，詔整肅儀衛，自皇后而下皆毋得迎謁。

translations.literal: Zhezong sent a messenger with the memorial racing to inform the Grand Empress Dowager; the next day an edict ordered the ceremonial guard rectified, and from the empress down none were permitted to meet and greet the procession.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong sent a messenger with the memorial racing to inform the Grand Empress Dowager. The next day an edict ordered the ceremonial guard rectified, and from the empress down none were permitted to meet and greet the procession.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部兼端明殿、翰林侍讀兩學士，爲禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was promoted to concurrent Academician of the Hall of Manifest Illumination and Hanlin Lecturer-in-Waiting in the Ministry of Rites, serving as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he was promoted to concurrent Academician of the Hall of Manifest Illumination and Hanlin Lecturer-in-Waiting in the Ministry of Rites, serving as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 高麗遣使請書，朝廷以故事盡許之。

translations.literal: Goryeo sent envoys requesting books; the court by precedent granted all they asked.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent envoys requesting books; the court by precedent granted all they asked.

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「漢東平王請諸子及《太史公書》，猶不肯予。

translations.literal: Shi said: "In Han times the Prince of Dongping requested copies of the Masters' works and Sima Qian's Records, and still was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said: "In Han times the Prince of Dongping requested copies of the Masters' works and Sima Qian's Records, and still was refused.

sentences.zh: 今高麗所請，有甚於此，其可予乎？」

translations.literal: What Goryeo now requests goes beyond that—how can it be granted?
translations.idiomatic: What Goryeo now requests goes beyond that—how can it be granted?

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 八年，宣仁后崩，哲宗親政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Empress Dowager Xuanren died and Zhezong personally took the reins of government.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Empress Dowager Xuanren died and Zhezong personally took the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 軾乞補外，以兩學士出知定州。

translations.literal: Shi requested a provincial post and was sent out as Academician of two halls to govern Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi requested a provincial post and was sent out as Academician of two halls to govern Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時國事將變，軾不得入辭。

translations.literal: At that time state affairs were about to change; Shi was not permitted a farewell audience.
translations.idiomatic: At that time state affairs were about to change; Su Shi was not permitted a farewell audience.

sentences.zh: 旣行，上書言：

translations.literal: After departing he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: After departing he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 「天下治亂，出於下情之通塞。

translations.literal: "Whether the realm is governed or in disorder depends on whether sentiments below can reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: "Whether the realm is governed or in disorder depends on whether sentiments below can reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 至治之極，小民皆能自通；

translations.literal: At the height of perfect order even common people can make themselves heard;
translations.idiomatic: At the height of perfect order even common people can make themselves heard;

sentences.zh: 迨於大亂，雖近臣不能自達。

translations.literal: when great disorder comes, even close ministers cannot make themselves heard.
translations.idiomatic: when great disorder comes, even close ministers cannot make themselves heard.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨御九年，除執政、臺諫外，未嘗與羣臣接。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has reigned nine years; apart from chief ministers and remonstrating censors, you have never met with the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned nine years; apart from chief ministers and remonstrating censors, you have never met with the officials.

sentences.zh: 今聽政之初，當以通下情、除壅蔽爲急務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your personal rule, opening channels below and removing obstruction should be urgent tasks.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of your personal rule, opening channels below and removing obstruction should be urgent tasks.

sentences.zh: 臣日侍帷幄，方當戍邊，顧不得一見而行，況疏遠小臣欲求自通，難矣。

translations.literal: I daily attend within the curtains, yet as I am about to guard the border I cannot even obtain one audience before departing—how much harder for distant minor officials who wish to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: I daily attend within the curtains, yet as I am about to guard the border I cannot even obtain one audience before departing—how much harder for distant minor officials who wish to be heard.

sentences.zh: 然臣不敢以不得對之故，不效愚忠。

translations.literal: Yet I dare not fail to offer loyal counsel because I cannot answer in person.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I dare not fail to offer loyal counsel because I cannot answer in person.

sentences.zh: 古之聖人將有爲也，必先處晦而觀明，處靜而觀動，則萬物之情，畢陳於前。

translations.literal: When the sages of old were about to act, they first placed themselves in obscurity to observe clarity, in stillness to observe movement—then the truth of all things was fully displayed before them.
translations.idiomatic: When the sages of old were about to act, they first placed themselves in obscurity to observe clarity, in stillness to observe movement—then the truth of all things was fully displayed before them.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖智絕人，春秋鼎盛。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sagely wisdom surpasses others, and you are in the prime of youth.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sagely wisdom surpasses others, and you are in the prime of youth.

sentences.zh: 臣願虛心循理，一切未有所爲，默觀庶事之利害，與羣臣之邪正。

translations.literal: I wish that you would empty your mind and follow reason, doing nothing at all for the moment, silently observing the gains and losses of affairs and the loyalty and treachery of officials.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that you would empty your mind and follow reason, doing nothing at all for the moment, silently observing the gains and losses of affairs and the loyalty and treachery of officials.

sentences.zh: 以三年爲期，俟得其實，然後應物而作。

translations.literal: Take three years as a term; wait until you know the truth, then respond to things and act.
translations.idiomatic: Take three years as a term; wait until you know the truth, then respond to things and act.

sentences.zh: 使旣作之後，天下無恨，陛下亦無悔。

translations.literal: Then after you act, the realm will have no regrets and Your Majesty will have no remorse.
translations.idiomatic: Then after you act, the realm will have no regrets and Your Majesty will have no remorse.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，陛下之有爲，惟憂太蚤，不患稍遲，亦已明矣。

translations.literal: Seen in this light, Your Majesty's acting need only fear being too early, not being slightly late—this is already clear.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, Your Majesty's acting need only fear being too early, not being slightly late—this is already clear.

sentences.zh: 臣恐急進好利之臣，輒勸陛下輕有改變，故進此說，敢望陛下留神，社稷宗廟之福，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: I fear that officials eager for advancement and profit will urge Your Majesty to change course lightly; therefore I offer this counsel. I dare hope Your Majesty will heed it—for the blessing of the state and ancestral temples, and the good fortune of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that officials eager for advancement and profit will urge Your Majesty to change course lightly; therefore I offer this counsel. I dare hope Your Majesty will heed it—for the blessing of the state and ancestral temples, and the good fortune of the realm."

sentences.zh: 定州軍政壞馳，諸衛卒驕惰不教，軍校蠶食其廩賜，前守不敢誰何。

translations.literal: Dingzhou military administration had fallen into ruin; guardsmen of the various guards were proud and lazy and untrained; military officers embezzled their grain stipends; previous prefects dared not challenge them.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou military administration had fallen into ruin. Guardsmen of the various guards were proud, lazy, and untrained; military officers embezzled their grain stipends; previous prefects dared not challenge them.

sentences.zh: 軾取貪污者配隸遠惡，繕脩營房，禁止飲博，軍中衣食稍足，乃部勒戰法，眾皆畏伏。

translations.literal: Shi assigned the corrupt to distant penal service, repaired barracks, and forbade drinking and gambling; once food and clothing in the army were somewhat sufficient, he drilled battle formations and all feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi assigned the corrupt to distant penal service, repaired barracks, and forbade drinking and gambling. Once food and clothing in the army were somewhat sufficient, he drilled battle formations and all feared and submitted.

sentences.zh: 然諸校業業不安，有卒史以贓訴其長，軾曰：「此事吾自治則可，聽汝告，軍中亂矣。」

translations.literal: But the officers were all uneasy; a clerk denounced his superior for embezzlement; Shi said: "This matter I can handle myself; if I let you denounce him, the army will fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: But the officers were all uneasy. A clerk denounced his superior for embezzlement. Su Shi said: "This matter I can handle myself; if I let you denounce him, the army will fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 立決配之，眾乃定。

translations.literal: He immediately sentenced and assigned him to penal service; the force then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sentenced and assigned him to penal service; the force then settled.

sentences.zh: 會春大閱，將吏久廢上下之分，軾命舉舊典，帥常服出帳中，將吏戎服執事。

translations.literal: When spring grand review came, officers and clerks had long abandoned hierarchy; Shi ordered the old regulations observed—the commander in ordinary dress emerged from the tent, officers and clerks in military dress performed their duties.
translations.idiomatic: When spring grand review came, officers and clerks had long abandoned hierarchy. Su Shi ordered the old regulations observed—the commander in ordinary dress emerged from the tent, officers and clerks in military dress performed their duties.

sentences.zh: 副總管王光祖自謂老將，恥之，稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Deputy Commander Wang Guangzu, considering himself a veteran general, felt shamed and claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Wang Guangzu, considering himself a veteran general, felt shamed and claimed illness and did not come.

sentences.zh: 軾召書吏使爲奏，光祖懼而出，訖事，無一慢者。

translations.literal: Shi summoned a clerk to draft a memorial; Guangzu feared and came out; when it was over, not one was remiss.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi summoned a clerk to draft a memorial; Guangzu feared and came out. When it was over, not one was remiss.

sentences.zh: 定人言：「自韓琦去後，不見此禮至今矣。」

translations.literal: People of Ding said: "Since Han Qi left, we have not seen such ceremony until now.
translations.idiomatic: People of Ding said: "Since Han Qi left, we have not seen such ceremony until now.

sentences.zh: 契丹久和，邊兵不可用，惟沿邊弓箭社與寇爲鄰，以戰射自衛，猶號精銳。

translations.literal: Khitan peace had lasted long; border troops were unusable; only the archery societies along the border, neighbors to bandits, trained in combat and archery for self-defense, were still called elite.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan peace had lasted long; border troops were unusable. Only the archery societies along the border, neighbors to bandits, trained in combat and archery for self-defense, were still called elite.

sentences.zh: 故相龐籍守邊，因俗立法。

translations.literal: Former Chancellor Pang Ji, when guarding the border, established law according to local custom.
translations.idiomatic: Former Chancellor Pang Ji, when guarding the border, established law according to local custom.

sentences.zh: 歲久法弛，又爲保甲所撓。

translations.literal: Over the years the law lapsed, and it was further disrupted by the baojia system.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years the law lapsed, and it was further disrupted by the baojia system.

sentences.zh: 軾奏免保甲及兩稅折變科配，不報。

translations.literal: Shi memorialized to exempt the baojia and the conversion and apportionment of the two taxes; no response came.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi memorialized to exempt the baojia and the conversion and apportionment of the two taxes, but no response came.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，御史論軾掌內外制日，所作詞命，以爲譏斥先朝。

translations.literal: At the start of Shaosheng, censors attacked Shi for the edicts he composed while holding inner and outer draft posts, claiming they mocked and condemned the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shaosheng, censors attacked Su Shi for the edicts he composed while holding inner and outer draft posts, claiming they mocked and condemned the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 遂以本官知英州，尋降一官，未至，貶寧遠軍節度副使，惠州安置。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent to govern Yingzhou at his existing rank, soon demoted one rank; before arriving he was demoted to Military Commissioner Vice Commissioner of Ningyuan Army and assigned to Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore sent to govern Yingzhou at his existing rank, soon demoted one rank. Before arriving he was demoted to Military Commissioner Vice Commissioner of Ningyuan Army and assigned to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 居三年，泊然無所蒂芥，人無賢愚，皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: He lived there three years, at ease without grievance; whether worthy or simple, all gave him their affection.
translations.idiomatic: He lived there three years, at ease without grievance. Whether worthy or simple, all gave him their affection.

sentences.zh: 又貶瓊州別駕，居昌化。

translations.literal: He was further demoted to Assistant Prefect of Qiongzhou and lived at Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was further demoted to Assistant Prefect of Qiongzhou and lived at Changhua.

sentences.zh: 昌化，故儋耳地，非人所居，藥餌皆無有。

translations.literal: Changhua was the old Dan'er territory—not a place fit for human habitation; medicines were wholly lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Changhua was the old Dan'er territory—not a place fit for human habitation. Medicines were wholly lacking.

sentences.zh: 初僦官屋以居，有司猶謂不可，軾遂買地築室，儋人運甓畚土以助之。

translations.literal: At first he rented official quarters to live in; the authorities still said this was not permitted; Shi then bought land and built a house; people of Dan transported bricks and baskets of earth to help.
translations.idiomatic: At first he rented official quarters to live in, but the authorities still said this was not permitted. Su Shi then bought land and built a house, and people of Dan transported bricks and baskets of earth to help.

sentences.zh: 獨與幼子過處，著書以爲樂，時時從其父老遊，若將終身。

translations.literal: He lived alone with his young son Guo, taking writing for pleasure, often keeping company with local elders as if he would end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: He lived alone with his young son Guo, taking writing for pleasure, often keeping company with local elders as if he would end his days there.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，移廉州，改舒州團練副使，徙永州。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended, he was moved to Lianzhou, changed to Vice Commissioner of Shuzhou Militia, then transferred to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended, he was moved to Lianzhou, changed to Vice Commissioner of Shuzhou Militia, then transferred to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 更三大赦，遂提舉玉局觀，復朝奉郎。

translations.literal: After three great amnesties he was appointed Superintendent of the Jade Bureau Abbey and restored to Gentleman for Attendant Service.
translations.idiomatic: After three great amnesties he was appointed Superintendent of the Jade Bureau Abbey and restored to Gentleman for Attendant Service.

sentences.zh: 軾自元祐以來，未嘗以歲課乞遷，故官止於此。

translations.literal: Since the Yuanyou era Shi had never sought promotion by annual merit reports, so his rank stopped here.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yuanyou era Su Shi had never sought promotion by annual merit reports, so his rank stopped here.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，卒于常州，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo he died at Changzhou, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo he died at Changzhou, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 軾與弟轍，師父洵爲文，旣而得之於天。

translations.literal: Shi and his brother Zhe studied writing under their father Xun, then received it from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi and his brother Zhe studied writing under their father Xun, then received it from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 嘗自謂：「作文如行雲流水，初無定質，但常行於所當行，止於所不可不止。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Writing is like drifting clouds and flowing water—it has no fixed form at first, but always moves where it should move and stops where it cannot but stop.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Writing is like drifting clouds and flowing water—it has no fixed form at first, but always moves where it should move and stops where it cannot but stop.

sentences.zh: 雖嬉笑怒駡之辭，皆可書而誦之。

translations.literal: Even words of jest, laughter, anger, and scolding could all be written down and recited.
translations.idiomatic: Even words of jest, laughter, anger, and scolding could all be written down and recited.

sentences.zh: 其體渾涵光芒，雄視百代，有文章以來，蓋亦鮮矣。

translations.literal: His style was full and luminous, towering over a hundred generations; since writing began, such cases have been rare.
translations.idiomatic: His style was full and luminous, towering over a hundred generations; since writing began, such cases have been rare.

sentences.zh: 洵晚讀《易》，作《易傳》未究，命軾述其志。

translations.literal: In his later years Xun read the Changes and began a Commentary on the Changes but did not finish; he charged Shi to carry out his intent.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Xun read the Book of Changes and began a Commentary on the Changes but did not finish; he charged Su Shi to carry out his intent.

sentences.zh: 軾成《易傳》，復作《論語說》；

translations.literal: Shi completed the Commentary on the Changes and also wrote Explanations of the Analects;
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi completed the Commentary on the Changes and also wrote Explanations of the Analects;

sentences.zh: 後居海南，作《書傳》；

translations.literal: later, living in Hainan, he wrote a Commentary on the Documents;
translations.idiomatic: later, living in Hainan, he wrote a Commentary on the Documents;

sentences.zh: 又有《東坡集》四十卷、《後集》二十卷、《奏議》十五卷、《內制》十卷、《外制》三卷、《和陶詩》四卷。

translations.literal: There were also Eastern Slope Collection in forty juan, Later Collection in twenty juan, Memorials and Discussions in fifteen juan, Inner Drafts in ten juan, Outer Drafts in three juan, and Poems in Harmony with Tao in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Eastern Slope Collection in forty juan, Later Collection in twenty juan, Memorials and Discussions in fifteen juan, Inner Drafts in ten juan, Outer Drafts in three juan, and Poems in Harmony with Tao in four juan.

sentences.zh: 一時文人如黃庭堅、晁補之、秦觀、張耒、陳師道，舉世未之識，軾待之如朋儔，未嘗以師資自予也。

translations.literal: Men of letters of the age such as Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi, Qin Guan, Zhang Lei, and Chen Shidao were unknown to the world; Shi treated them as peers and never assumed the role of master.
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters of the age such as Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi, Qin Guan, Zhang Lei, and Chen Shidao were unknown to the world; Su Shi treated them as peers and never assumed the role of master.

sentences.zh: 自爲舉子至出入侍從，必以愛君爲本，忠規讜論，挺挺大節，羣臣無出其右。

translations.literal: From his days as an examination candidate to his service in attendance, he always took love of the ruler as his foundation; loyal remonstrance and forthright counsel, upright integrity—among the officials none surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: From his days as an examination candidate to his service in attendance, he always took love of the ruler as his foundation. His loyal remonstrance and forthright counsel, his upright integrity—among the officials none surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 但爲小人忌惡擠排，不使安於朝廷之上。

translations.literal: But petty men envied and hated him and drove him out, not allowing him to rest at ease in court.
translations.idiomatic: But petty men envied and hated him and drove him out, not allowing him to rest at ease at court.

sentences.zh: 高宗卽位，贈資政殿學士，以其孫符爲禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended, Shi was posthumously granted Academician of the Hall for Propagation of Governance, and his grandson Fu was made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended, Su Shi was posthumously granted Academician of the Hall for Propagation of Governance, and his grandson Fu was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 又以其文置左右，讀之終日忘倦，謂爲文章之宗，親制集贊，賜其曾孫嶠。

translations.literal: He also kept Shi's writings at hand, reading them all day without tiring, calling him patriarch of letters; he personally composed a preface for the collected works and granted it to his great-grandson Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He also kept Su Shi's writings at hand, reading them all day without tiring, calling him patriarch of letters. He personally composed a preface for the collected works and granted it to his great-grandson Qiao.

sentences.zh: 遂崇贈太師，諡「文忠」。

translations.literal: Shi was then posthumously elevated to Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title "Loyal in Letters."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi was then posthumously elevated to Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title "Loyal in Letters."

sentences.zh: 軾三子：邁、迨、過，俱善爲文。

translations.literal: Shi had three sons: Mai, Dai, and Guo—all skilled in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi had three sons: Mai, Dai, and Guo—all skilled in writing.

sentences.zh: 邁，駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: Mai was Vice Director of the Office of Imperial Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Mai served as Vice Director of the Office of Imperial Equipage.

sentences.zh: 迨，承務郎。

translations.literal: Dai was Gentleman for Managing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dai served as Gentleman for Managing Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子 過

translations.literal: Son: Guo
translations.idiomatic: Son: Guo

sentences.zh: 過，字叔黨。

translations.literal: Guo, styled Shudang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo, whose style name was Shudang.

sentences.zh: 軾知杭州，過年十九，以詩賦解兩浙路，禮部試下。

translations.literal: When Shi governed Hangzhou, Guo was nineteen; by poetry and rhapsody he passed the Two Zhe circuit preliminary and fell short at the Ministry of Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi governed Hangzhou, Guo was nineteen. By poetry and rhapsody he passed the Two Zhe circuit preliminary but fell short at the Ministry of Rites examination.

sentences.zh: 及軾為兵部尚書，任右承務郎。

translations.literal: When Shi became Minister of War, Guo was appointed Right Gentleman for Attending Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi became Minister of War, Guo was appointed Right Gentleman for Attending Affairs.

sentences.zh: 軾帥定武，謫知英州，貶惠州，遷儋耳，漸徙廉、永，獨過侍之。

translations.literal: When Shi commanded Dingzhou, was demoted to govern Yingzhou, banished to Huizhou, moved to Dan'er, and gradually transferred to Lian and Yong, Guo alone attended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi commanded Dingzhou, was demoted to govern Yingzhou, banished to Huizhou, moved to Dan'er, and gradually transferred to Lian and Yong, Guo alone attended him.

sentences.zh: 凡生理晝夜寒暑所須者，一身百為，不知其難。

translations.literal: For everything needed in daily life day and night through summer and winter, he alone did a hundred tasks and did not know the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: For everything needed in daily life day and night through summer and winter, he alone did a hundred tasks without seeming to know the hardship.

sentences.zh: 初至海上，為文曰《志隱》，軾覽之曰：「吾可以安於島夷矣。」

translations.literal: When he first reached the sea, he wrote an essay called "Record of Hidden Intent"; Shi read it and said: "I can now settle at ease among these island barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When he first reached the sea, he wrote an essay called "Record of Hidden Intent." Su Shi read it and said: "I can now settle at ease among these island barbarians.

sentences.zh: 因命作《孔子弟子別傳》。

translations.literal: He then ordered him to write Separate Biographies of the Disciples of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered him to write Separate Biographies of the Disciples of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 軾卒於常州，過葬軾汝州郟城小峨眉山，遂家潁昌，營湖陰水竹數畝，名曰「小斜川」，自號「斜川居士」。

translations.literal: When Shi died at Changzhou, Guo buried him at Little Emei Mountain in Jia County, Ruzhou; he then made his home at Yingchang, laid out several mu of waters and bamboo by the lake, naming it "Little Xie Stream," and styled himself "Recluse of Xie Stream."
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi died at Changzhou, Guo buried him at Little Emei Mountain in Jia County, Ruzhou. He then made his home at Yingchang, laid out several mu of waters and bamboo by the lake, naming it "Little Xie Stream," and styled himself "Recluse of Xie Stream."

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 初監太原府稅，次知潁昌府郾城縣，皆以法令罷。

translations.literal: At first he supervised taxes at Taiyuan Prefecture, then governed Yancheng County in Yingchang Prefecture—both times he was dismissed for legal violations.
translations.idiomatic: At first he supervised taxes at Taiyuan Prefecture, then governed Yancheng County in Yingchang Prefecture—both times he was dismissed for legal violations.

sentences.zh: 晚權通判中山府。

translations.literal: In his later years he served as acting Vice Prefect of Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he served as acting Vice Prefect of Zhongshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有《斜川集》二十卷。

translations.literal: He had Xie Stream Collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left Xie Stream Collection in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 其《思子臺賦》、《颶風賦》早行於世。

translations.literal: His "Rhapsody on the Terrace for Thinking of One's Son" and "Rhapsody on the Hurricane" circulated early in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His "Rhapsody on the Terrace for Thinking of One's Son" and "Rhapsody on the Hurricane" circulated early in the world.

sentences.zh: 時稱為「小坡」，蓋以軾為「大坡」也。

translations.literal: He was called at the time "Little Slope," because Shi was called "Great Slope."
translations.idiomatic: He was called at the time "Little Slope," because Su Shi was called "Great Slope."

sentences.zh: 其叔轍每稱過孝，以訓宗族。

translations.literal: His uncle Zhe often praised Guo's filial piety to instruct the clan.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zhe often praised Guo's filial piety to instruct the clan.

sentences.zh: 且言：「吾兄遠居海上，惟成就此兒能文也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "My elder brother lives far on the sea; only in raising this boy to write well has he succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "My elder brother lives far on the sea; only in raising this boy to write well has he succeeded.

sentences.zh: 七子：籥、籍、節、笈、篳、篴、箾。

translations.literal: He had seven sons: Yue, Ji, Jie, Ji, Bi, Di, and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Yue, Ji, Jie, Ji, Bi, Di, and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 論曰：蘇軾自爲童子時，士有傳石介《慶曆聖德詩》至蜀中者，軾歷舉詩中所言韓、富、杜、范諸賢以問其師。

translations.literal: Commentator's note: When Su Shi was still a child, a scholar brought Shi Jie's "Holy Virtue Poem of the Qingli Era" to Shu; Shi listed the worthies Han, Fu, Du, and Fan mentioned in the poem and asked his teacher about them.
translations.idiomatic: Commentator's note: When Su Shi was still a child, a scholar brought Shi Jie's "Holy Virtue Poem of the Qingli Era" to Shu. Su Shi listed the worthies Han, Fu, Du, and Fan mentioned in the poem and asked his teacher about them.

sentences.zh: 師怪而語之，則曰：「正欲識是諸人耳。」

translations.literal: His teacher, surprised, asked why; he said: "I just want to know these men.
translations.idiomatic: His teacher, surprised, asked why. He said: "I just want to know these men.

sentences.zh: 蓋已有頡頏當世賢哲之意。

translations.literal: Thus he already had the intent to rival the sages of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly he already had the intent to rival the sages of his age.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，父子兄弟至京師，一日而聲名赫然，動于四方。

translations.literal: At twenty, father, sons, and brothers reached the capital; in a single day their fame blazed forth and stirred the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty, father, sons, and brothers reached the capital. In a single day their fame blazed forth and stirred the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 旣而登上第，擢詞科，入掌書命，出典方州。

translations.literal: Thereafter they passed the highest examinations, were selected for the rhyme-prose category, entered to hold drafting posts, and went out to govern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they passed the highest examinations, were selected for the rhyme-prose category, entered to hold drafting posts, and went out to govern provinces.

sentences.zh: 器識之閎偉，議論之卓犖，文章之雄雋，政事之精明，四者皆能以特立之志爲之主，而以邁往之氣輔之。

translations.literal: The grandeur of his capacity and insight, the excellence of his discourse, the bold excellence of his writing, the clarity of his governance—in all four he had exceptional will as master and forward-moving spirit as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The grandeur of his capacity and insight, the excellence of his discourse, the bold excellence of his writing, the clarity of his governance—in all four he had exceptional will as master and forward-moving spirit as assistant.

sentences.zh: 故意之所向，言足以達其有猷，行足以遂其有爲。

translations.literal: Therefore where his intent was directed, his words sufficed to convey his designs and his actions sufficed to accomplish his deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore where his intent was directed, his words sufficed to convey his designs and his actions sufficed to accomplish his deeds.

sentences.zh: 至於禍患之來，節義足以固其有守，皆志與氣所爲也。

translations.literal: When disaster came, integrity and righteousness sufficed to fortify what he upheld—all was the work of will and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster came, integrity and righteousness sufficed to fortify what he upheld—all was the work of will and spirit.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初讀軾、轍制策，退而喜曰：「朕今日爲子孫得兩宰相矣。」

translations.literal: When Renzong first read the policy essays of Shi and Zhe, he withdrew and said with delight: "Today I have obtained two chancellors for my descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong first read the policy essays of Su Shi and Zhe, he withdrew and said with delight: "Today I have obtained two chancellors for my descendants.

sentences.zh: 神宗尤愛其文，宮中讀之，膳進忘食，稱爲天下奇才。

translations.literal: Shenzong especially loved Shi's writing; reading it in the palace he forgot his meal at serving time and called him the singular genius of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong especially loved Su Shi's writing; reading it in the palace he forgot his meal at serving time and called him the singular genius of the realm.

sentences.zh: 二君皆有以知軾，而軾卒不得大用。

translations.literal: Both rulers had the means to know Shi, yet Shi ultimately was not greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Both rulers had the means to know Su Shi, yet Su Shi ultimately was not greatly employed.

sentences.zh: 一歐陽脩先識之，其名遂與之齊，豈非軾之所長不可掩抑者，天下之至公也，相不相有命焉，嗚呼！

translations.literal: When Ouyang Xiu first recognized him, his name rose level with Xiu's—is this not proof that Shi's strengths could not be suppressed, the utmost fairness of the realm? Whether one becomes chancellor or not is a matter of fate—alas!
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Xiu first recognized him, his name rose level with Xiu's—is this not proof that Su Shi's strengths could not be suppressed, the utmost fairness of the realm? Whether one becomes chancellor or not is a matter of fate—alas!

sentences.zh: 軾不得相，又豈非幸歟？

translations.literal: That Shi did not become chancellor—was that not also fortune?
translations.idiomatic: That Su Shi did not become chancellor—was that not also fortune?

sentences.zh: 或謂：「軾稍自韜戢，雖不獲柄用，亦當免禍。」

translations.literal: Some say: "If Shi had restrained himself slightly, though he might not have wielded power, he should still have avoided disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Some say: "If Su Shi had restrained himself slightly, though he might not have wielded power, he should still have avoided disaster.

sentences.zh: 雖然，假令軾以是而易其所爲，尚得爲軾哉？

translations.literal: Nevertheless, if Shi had changed what he did on that account, could he still have been Shi?
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, if Su Shi had changed what he did on that account, could he still have been Su Shi?
